ENAM Holdings - AI Engineer Build Challenge 
FINN: Financial Investment Agent 
Release Date: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 
Deadline: Sunday, November 1, 2026  
Deliverable: A mobile-first working prototype + repository + covering note 
What we're evaluating: How you build, what you choose to build, and the creativity and judgment 
behind it — not completeness or polish. 
Companion file. A separate reference document accompanies this brief — “Reference: 
Announcement Categories & Financial Glossary.” It lists the corporate-announcement categories 
and explains every financial term and document type mentioned here in plain English. You do not 
need any prior finance knowledge — lean on it freely. 
About this challenge 
We are a public-markets investment firm. We run lean — a small team makes high-conviction 
decisions and lives with the outcomes. We're building an AI-powered intelligence layer for how we 
invest, and this challenge is a taste of the real problem. You do not need finance or public-markets 
expertise: the domain is scaffolded for you, and the companion reference document explains 
everything financial referenced here. We're hiring for building ability, product instinct, and 
creativity. 
The problem 
An investor today is drowning in information — prices, filings, announcements, results, macro. It 
never stops, and most of it doesn't matter. The scarce skill is not aggregating information. It's 
filtering it: surfacing the few things that actually matter and burying everything else, beautifully. 
Build something that becomes part of a daily investor's workflow — a product they reach for 
through the day that saves them time and shows them only what's important. 
What you'll build 
FINN - a mobile-first financial investment agent. It works in two modes of interaction: 
● Push — it proactively tells you what changed and why you should care. 
● Pull — you ask it to research or analyse something on demand. 
We guide you on the backend (the data). The frontend — the product, the interaction model, the 
design — is deliberately yours. That's where we most want to see how you think. 
Your companies 
● Portfolio: choose your own mock portfolio of 15–20 NSE/BSE-listed companies. Pick a mix 
that makes for an interesting demo — different sectors and sizes will show more. 
● Ad-hoc research: in addition, pick a handful of companies (say 3–5), which can be outside 
your portfolio, to demo the on-demand research on. 

===== PAGE 2 =====
ENAM Holdings Pvt. Ltd.  
2
● Build the engine to generalise. The research must not be hard-wired to your demo set — 
build it so it works on any NSE ticker where the data is available. We may point it at a 
company you didn't pick. 
The backend — your data sources (guided) 
Three sources. Get them working; don't over-engineer them — this part is plumbing, not the point. 
● Price & volume (end-of-day) for your portfolio. Freely scrapable at end of day from public 
sources — Yahoo Finance is the usual starting point (the yfinance Python library; Indian 
tickers use .NS for NSE and .BO for BSE, e.g. RELIANCE.NS). Anything equivalent works. 
● Corporate announcements / filings from NSE/BSE for those stocks. A classification of 
announcement types is provided in the companion reference document — use it, adapt it, or 
ignore it. It's there to orient you, not to constrain you. 
● Company fundamentals — annual reports and concall (earnings-call) transcripts, both 
available as links on screener.in (or the company's investor-relations site). 
The frontend — your canvas 
This is the heart of the challenge. Give us part of a real investor's daily workflow, built beautifully. 
The items below are examples of the kinds of things that help — illustrations, not a checklist. What 
you choose to build, and how, is the signal. 
Push — the app reaches out to you 
Push is the app telling you what changed without being asked. Think of it in two flavours: 
1. A windowed digest. For a time window I choose — by default the last 24 hours, but let me pick 
the period — show me every corporate filing/announcement across my portfolio, filtered and 
prioritised so I see what matters first and the routine stuff is collapsed or hidden. 
2. Triggered alerts. Tell me the moment something crosses a threshold, for example: 
● a material announcement of a type I care about (results, M&A, management change, and so 
on); or 
● an unusual move in my end-of-day data — e.g. volume more than ~2× its recent average, or 
a price move beyond ±X% in a day. Make the threshold configurable: the point is that I 
decide what "unusual" means and the app watches for it. 
How a pushed item should be presented — two examples we love; the rest is your call: 
● Management change → don't just say "CFO resigned." Pull a short background/bio of the 
incoming person (e.g. from LinkedIn) so I instantly know who they are and where they came 
from. 
● Quarterly results → take the actual results filing and give me a first cut of the headline 
numbers — Revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT — this quarter vs. last quarter (QoQ) and vs. the 
same quarter a year ago (YoY). Those four are defined in the reference document. 
For every other announcement type, decide what earns my attention: a one-line summary next to 
the filing, or just the filing surfaced at the right priority. That judgment is the point. 
Pull — you ask it to dig in 
Pull is on-demand analysis of a company, grounded in its fundamentals (annual reports + concall 
transcripts). Below are eight kinds of output a good research view might contain — we spell them

out because you may not have a finance background. Treat them as a menu: pick what you build and 
how deep you go. Each is explained further in the reference document. 
● Business snapshot — what the company does, its segments, revenue mix. 
● Financial snapshot — current headline numbers (revenue, margins, PAT, key ratios) at a 
glance. 
● Trajectory — the multi-year direction: what's growing, what's compressing. 
● Balance sheet — debt, leverage, working-capital cycle, funding structure. 
● Cash quality — cash-flow trend and cash conversion: do profits turn into cash? 
● Narrative vs. numbers — where management's story and the actual financials agree or 
diverge. 
● Guidance — what management has explicitly guided on headline numbers (growth, margins, 
capex). 
● Bull vs. bear — a tight case each way. 
Worked example — numbers vs. narrative: take the last four quarters and, against management's 
own headline guidance and growth commentary, tell me what was promised vs. what was actually 
delivered. This is the difference between summarising management and analysing them — and it's 
the kind of thing we value most. 
One discipline for the pull side: ground it in the primary sources (annual reports + transcripts). No 
broker notes, no news, no research reports, and don't lean on the model's own outside knowledge 
of the company. Differentiated signal lives in primary data; secondary commentary is where it gets 
noisy. (Push-side enrichment like a person's professional background is a different thing and 
completely fine.) 
The interaction model — experiment 
How the investor interacts with all of this is entirely up to you, and we strongly encourage you to 
experiment. Chat, voice, a copilot, a dashboard, or something we haven't thought of — try more 
than the obvious. Everything mobile-first. The best submissions will show a point of view about how 
an investor should interact with this, not just what data to show. 
The bar — no AI slop 
Whatever you build: core, concise, beautifully presented, and interactive. It should save the investor 
time and show them what's important — and feel like a product someone thought hard about, not a 
model filling a template. Density and design both count. 
Tools, models & cost 
● No restriction on models. Use anything — open-source, local, or any commercial provider. 
Pick the right tool for each step; that choice is part of what we're evaluating. 
● This is comfortably doable on free tiers — you do not need to spend to compete. 
● Efficiency earns bonus points. The less you spend to achieve the same result, the better. 
Smart model routing (cheap models for bulk extraction, a stronger model only where 
reasoning demands it), caching, and chunking are exactly the instincts we're looking for. 
Scope, and how we grade 
● The deliverable is a mobile-first working prototype. We grade creativity, product sense, 
judgment, and architecture — not completeness.

===== PAGE 1 =====
Reference: Announcement Categories & 
Financial Glossary 
A companion to the Build Challenge brief. You do not need a finance background — this document 
explains the corporate-announcement categories and the financial terms and documents referenced 
in the main brief. Lean on it freely. 
 
1. Corporate announcement categories 
How we classify the announcements companies file with the exchanges. In the main brief this is 
offered as guidance only — you may use it, adapt it, or ignore it. 
Category 
What goes in it 
results 
Quarterly/annual results, the board meeting approving them, results 
decks and shareholder letters, and ads confirming results were 
published. 
M&A 
Any acquisition, merger, demerger, or joint venture — including 
investing in a subsidiary, or selling a stake in one. 
fund_raise 
Raising money from outside investors — rights issues, QIPs, preferential 
allotments, buybacks, or debt like commercial paper. 
management_change 
Any change at the top — a CEO, CFO, MD, or director joining, resigning, 
or retiring. 
litigation 
Lawsuits, regulatory orders, fines, warnings, or insolvency/restructuring 
proceedings. 
insider_trading 
A promoter or insider buying/selling their own personal shareholding. 
earnings_call 
Anything about the investor conference call — the notice, the 
transcript, or the recording link. 
investor_meetings 
One-on-one or small-group meetings with specific investors/funds, or 
attending an investor conference. 
credit_rating 
A rating agency assigning, upgrading, downgrading, or reaffirming a 
credit rating. 
dividend 
A cash dividend being declared, with its record date. 
bonus_split 
A bonus issue or stock split — share count changes but no cash comes 
to you. 
capex 
Approving spend on a new plant, facility, or capacity expansion. 
press_release 
General news — order wins, new products, partnerships, rumour 
clarifications — not covered by another category. 
postal_ballot 
Shareholders voting by postal ballot — the notice and the result. 
agm_egm 
Annual or Extraordinary General Meeting — the notice and the result. 
pledging 
A promoter pledging, releasing, or changing the pledge status of shares. 
unclassified 
Routine, low-relevance paperwork — ESOP allotments, compliance 
certificates, ESG reports, auditor appointments — that doesn't 
materially move the stock. 
 

===== PAGE 2 =====
2. Documents you'll work with 
Annual Report (AR) — A company's yearly disclosure. Contains the business overview, management 
discussion, audited financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash-flow), and the notes and auditor's 
report. The single richest primary source. 
Quarterly results — The financial results a company publishes every quarter (revenue, profit, etc.), 
filed with the exchanges. Less detailed than the annual report but far more current. 
Concall / earnings-call transcript — A quarterly call where management discusses the results and 
answers analysts' questions. The transcript is where you find guidance, tone, and what analysts are 
pressing on. 
Investor presentation — A slide deck management releases (often with results) framing strategy, 
KPIs, and segment performance in their own words. 
Exchange filing / announcement — Any disclosure a listed company files with NSE/BSE — the raw 
feed the push side monitors. 
screener.in — A widely-used site that consolidates a company's annual reports, concall transcripts, 
and standardised multi-year financials in one place — the easiest place to fetch fundamentals. 
Primary vs. secondary data — Primary data comes straight from the company (filings, reports, 
transcripts). Secondary data is other people's commentary on it (news, broker notes, research 
reports). The pull/analysis side of this challenge must use primary data only. 
3. Headline financial terms 
Revenue — Total sales — the top line of the P&L; the money coming in from selling goods/services. 
EBITDA — Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation & Amortisation. A rough proxy for operating 
profitability — how profitable the core business is before financing and accounting effects. 
PBT — Profit Before Tax — profit after all costs and interest but before income tax. 
PAT — Profit After Tax — the bottom line; what's left for shareholders after tax. Also called "net 
profit." 
Margin — A profit figure as a % of revenue (e.g. EBITDA margin = EBITDA ÷ revenue). Shows how 
much of each rupee of sales becomes profit. 
QoQ (quarter-on-quarter) — This quarter compared with the immediately previous quarter. 
YoY (year-on-year) — This quarter compared with the same quarter a year earlier — the usual way 
to strip out seasonality. 
4. Balance-sheet, cash & ratio terms 
Balance sheet — A snapshot of what a company owns (assets) and owes (liabilities) at a point in 
time, plus shareholders' equity. 
Debt / leverage — Money the company has borrowed. "Leverage" describes how much debt it 
carries relative to its equity or earnings — more debt means more risk. 
Debt-to-Equity (D/E) — A leverage ratio: total debt ÷ shareholders' equity. Higher = more reliance 
on borrowing. 
Working-capital cycle — The cash tied up in day-to-day operations — inventory and money owed by 
customers, minus money owed to suppliers. A lengthening cycle can quietly drain cash. 
Cash flow — The actual cash moving in and out, as opposed to accounting profit. "Cash from 
operations" is the cash the core business generates. 

===== PAGE 3 =====
Cash conversion — How well accounting profit turns into real cash. Persistent profit without 
matching cash flow is a red flag. 
Free cash flow (FCF) — Cash from operations minus capital spending — the cash genuinely left over. 
ROCE / ROE — Return on Capital Employed / Return on Equity — how much profit the company 
generates per rupee of capital / shareholders' money. Higher is generally better. 
Contingent liabilities — Potential future obligations (e.g. disputed taxes, guarantees) disclosed in 
the notes — not yet on the balance sheet but worth watching. 
Related-party transactions (RPTs) — Deals between the company and its own promoters/insiders or 
their other businesses — legitimate but a place to watch for value leaking out. 
Auditor's qualification — When the auditor flags a concern about the accounts rather than signing 
off cleanly — a signal to dig deeper. 
5. Corporate-action & market terms 
NSE / BSE — India's two main stock exchanges (National / Bombay Stock Exchange). Listed 
companies file their announcements here. 
Ticker / symbol — A stock's short code. On Yahoo Finance, Indian tickers add .NS (NSE) or .BO (BSE) 
— e.g. RELIANCE.NS. 
Market capitalisation — The total market value of a company's shares (share price × number of 
shares). A rough measure of company size. 
Promoter — The controlling shareholder / founding group of an Indian listed company. 
Pledging — A promoter using their own shares as collateral for a loan. Heavy pledging is a risk signal. 
Material announcement — A disclosure significant enough to potentially move the stock, as 
opposed to routine compliance paperwork. 
Guidance — Management's own stated forward expectations — for growth, margins, capex, and so 
on. 
Capex (capital expenditure) — Spending on long-term assets like new plants or capacity. 
Dividend — A cash payout to shareholders from profits. 
Record date — The cut-off date deciding who's eligible for a dividend, bonus, or split. 
Bonus issue / stock split — Corporate actions that increase your share count without any cash 
changing hands; each share is worth proportionally less. 
Buyback — A company buying back its own shares from the market, usually returning surplus cash 
to shareholders. 
Rights issue / QIP / preferential allotment — Ways a company raises fresh equity — from existing 
shareholders (rights), from institutions (QIP = Qualified Institutional Placement), or to specific 
investors (preferential allotment). 
EOD (end-of-day) — Data taken after market close — the daily close price and traded volume used 
on the push side.

I should pick stocks with recent results announcements to showcase that part of the demo — checking NSE announcements from the last few days and curating a mix of sectors, some with fresh earnings and some with management changes, keeps the mock portfolio plausible yet compelling. For the research demo set, companies with strong concall transcripts like DIXON, PERSISTENT, TITAN, POLYCAB, and ASIANPAINT make sense, since the engine needs to generalize well. Now I'm sketching the backend module structure, starting with a shared HTTP client module for making requests with browser-like headers. Adding retry logic and disk caching... For the NSE source module, I'm planning functions to fetch announcements (symbol, company name, subject, summary text, PDF link, timestamp, industry) and to pull the full equity list from NSE's CSV. For yahoo.py I'm planning an EOD price fetcher returning OHLCV data, then deriving signals like daily return, volume vs 20-day average, proximity to 52-week highs/lows, and price gaps. For screener.py, I'm mapping out how to parse the company page: name, about section, key ratios, quarterly and financial statement tables, shareholding pattern (promoter holding, pledging), and document links for annual reports and concall transcripts/presentations. Now I'm thinking through classify.py — building a mapping of NSE announcement subject categories (board meeting outcomes, financial results, management changes, analyst meets, credit ratings, acquisitions, allotments, press releases, investor presentations, etc.) so each filing can be tagged with an appropriate type for downstream processing. I'm also assigning materiality weights per category — actual financials scoring highest, intimations lower, management changes varying by role, credit rating moves, dividends, capex, and so on — then adjusting these base scores by portfolio relevance, the user's mute/digest preferences, and same-day price reaction magnitude. Then I need to handle dedup logic (same filing posted to both exchanges, multiple attachments, similar filings grouped together) and collapse everything into three action tiers: Act, Know, and Routine based on score thresholds. For the results-processing module specifically, I'm designing a pipeline that takes a results announcement PDF, extracts text from the first few pages, locates the financial results table, then sends it to a fast LLM to pull out structured JSON — consolidated vs standalone basis, currency unit, and per-period figures like revenue, EBITDA, PBT, tax, and PAT across the current quarter, previous quarter, and year-ago comparisons. I'm working out how to compute EBITDA deterministically from the extracted components rather than trusting the LLM's math, flag exceptional items separately, calculate QoQ/YoY changes, and cross-validate totals against Screener's quarterly data as a sanity check. I also need a fallback path using Screener's numbers alone when there's no LLM extraction, and special handling for banks/NBFCs where "EBITDA" doesn't apply — showing total income and operating profit instead. I'm also realizing results PDFs often have both standalone and consolidated figures (prefer consolidated), and some PDFs are scanned images with no extractable text, so I need a fallback for those cases too, possibly leveraging multimodal PDF input if the API supports it. For management changes, I'm planning for the LLM to extract structured data from the SEBI LODR "Brief Profile" annexure—person, role, change type, effective date, bio details—and then enrich it with a Wikipedia summary lookup and a LinkedIn search deep link, since the brief wants a short background on incoming people but actual LinkedIn scraping isn't viable. For other material announcements, I'm reusing NSE's attchmntText field directly as a free one-line summary when it's substantive, only falling back to the LLM for generic Act-tier text like "Please find attached..." to keep costs down. For alerts, I'm designing rules around price moves (≥4%), volume spikes (2x the 20-day average), category-based triggers (results, M&A, management changes), and 52-week highs/lows, evaluated over EOD data windows. The key insight is correlating triggered alerts with same-day or prior-evening filings so the alert explains itself — e.g., "TCS −5.1% on 2.4× avg volume — coincides with Q2 results filed at 16:05." I'm also noting that web push notifications need HTTPS, which complicates a local LAN demo running over HTTP. Given that constraint, I'll skip OS-level push and instead build an in-app alert inbox plus an optional browser Notification API that works when running on localhost. A "Simulate market close" button could trigger an EOD scan and surface in-app notifications on demand, which is more reliable for a live demo than waiting for a real market event. Now I'm sketching out the research module — pulling screener financial data and documents like annual reports and concall transcripts for a given symbol, then structuring it into sections like a business snapshot (from screener's "about" text sourced from company/BSE profiles) and segment revenue mix extracted from annual report notes via LLM. For AR extraction, I'd download the latest AR PDF and use PyMuPDF since it's fast even on large 300-page files, then search for pages mentioning "segment" and "revenue" tables, running a fast-tier LLM pass to extract the segment mix and caching the result, falling back to the about text if extraction fails. The financial snapshot would be deterministic, pulling TTM revenue, EBITDA margin, PAT, ROCE, ROE, P/E, market cap, and D/E directly from screener, while the trajectory section would compute multi-year CAGRs (3y/5y/10y) for revenue/EBITDA/PAT, margin trends, sparkline charts, and a templated narrative line. The balance sheet section would also be deterministic, covering borrowings and related metrics. For cash quality, I'm figuring out CFO vs PAT conversion over 5 years and FCF calculation, but capex isn't directly separable from screener's "Cash from Investing" line since it bundles capex with investments. I realize the schedules API (`/api/company/{id}/schedules/?parent=Cash+from+Investing+Activity&section=cash-flow`) can break this down into "Fixed assets purchased" and "Fixed assets sold," which solves the capex problem — I just need to check whether that endpoint works without being logged in. Next, for guidance tracking, I'm planning to pull the last 4 concall transcripts, use a fast LLM to extract forward-looking statements (filtering for relevant keywords to save tokens) into structured items with metric, target, period, quote, speaker, and source, then use a stronger model to compare these promises against actual delivered performance from quarterly data, producing a credibility-scored ledger with citations. For narrative-vs-numbers, bull/bear cases, and the Q&A assistant, I'm settling on a model routing strategy: cheap/fast models for extraction, stronger models for synthesis with citation validation (dropping any uncited claims), caching by document hash and prompt version, and keyword-prefiltered chunking plus BM25 retrieval for Q&A to avoid embedding costs. Given the scope, I'm thinking "thin-but-working beats broad-but-broken" — stage the build so each piece works end-to-end before layering more on. My plan: start with a skeleton plus .env setup and a model check, then build the data layer (NSE announcements, Yahoo EOD, screener parsing, PDF text extraction) and test with real calls before pushing further. From there I'll build the pull engine (classification, scoring, digest API, alerts, results/management extraction), then the corresponding frontend pieces (Brief, Alerts, Settings, Results cards), followed by the deeper research dossier work (deterministic sections first, then LLM-driven sections for guidance comparisons and bull/bear framing) plus an Ask feature and its UI. Polish comes last: text-to-speech, swipe triage, PWA manifest, dark theme, loading states, caching/snapshot mode, and finally documentation, screenshots, and packaging everything into a zip.   "command": "$env:PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'; Set-Location Q:\\sp\\finn\\backend; @'\nfrom datetime import date, timedelta\nfrom concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor\nfrom app.sources import nse, yahoo\nfrom app.engine.classify import classify\ncands = \"RELIANCE HDFCBANK ICICIBANK SBIN AXISBANK KOTAKBANK TCS INFY HCLTECH WIPRO LT BHARTIARTL ITC HINDUNILVR NESTLEIND SUNPHARMA DRREDDY CIPLA LUPIN MARUTI M&M TATAMOTORS EICHERMOT BAJAJ-AUTO HEROMOTOCO TVSMOTOR BAJFINANCE TITAN DIXON POLYCAB HAVELLS PERSISTENT KPITTECH COFORGE TRENT DMART HAL BEL COCHINSHIP ETERNAL NYKAA PAYTM SUZLON TATAPOWER ADANIENT JSWSTEEL TATASTEEL VEDL COALINDIA ONGC CDSL BSE ANGELONE ASIANPAINT PIDILITIND ULTRACEMCO APOLLOHOSP MAXHEALTH IDEA IRFC IREDA DEEPAKNTR SRF\".split()\nend = date.today(); start = end - timedelta(days=7)\ndef scan(s):\n    try:\n        a = nse.announcements(s, start, end)\n    except Exception as e:\n        return s, None, str(e)\n    cats = [classify(x[\"desc\"], x[\"text\"]) for x in a]\n    top = sorted(set((c[\"category\"]+\"/\"+c[\"subtype\"]) for c in cats if c[\"score\"]>=45))\n    try:\n        h = yahoo.history(s, \"3mo\"); cs = h[\"candles\"]\n        rets = [(cs[i][\"c\"]/cs[i-1][\"c\"]-1)*100 for i in range(len(cs)-5, len(cs))]\n        vm = []\n        for i in range(len(cs)-5, len(cs)):\n            avg = sum(c[\"v\"] for c in cs[i-20:i])/20\n            vm.append(cs[i][\"v\"]/avg if avg else 0)\n        mv = f\"maxabs5d={max(rets, key=abs):+.1f}% maxvol5d={max(vm):.1f}x last={rets[-1]:+.1f}%\"\n    except Exception as e:\n        mv = f\"yahoo err {e}\"\n    return s, (len(a), top), mv\nwith ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:\n    for s, info, mv in ex.map(scan, cands):\n        print(f\"{s:11s} {mv:45s} {info}\")\n'@ | .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -",
  "description": "Scan candidate stocks for recent events",
  "initial_wait": 180
}

Results look mostly solid: 9 of 10 got real numbers from exchange XBRL. KPITTECH fell back to Screener since the integrated filing wasn't live yet (results just posted), which is a reasonable fallback given no PDF URL was passed. Now checking BAJFINANCE, an NBFC, for similar issues. For NBFCs, "Revenue from operations" isn't a single line — it's broken into interest income, fees/commission income, net gains on fair value changes, etc., rolling up to "Total revenue from operations" and then "Total income." Also EBITDA doesn't make sense for NBFCs since finance costs (interest expense) are their core cost, not overhead — similar to banks. I should detect NBFC-style filings (e.g. by presence of "impairment on financial instruments" or similar line items) and switch to showing "Total income" and pre-provision metrics instead of a misleading EBITDA figure. Now I'm planning to add an `nbfc` boolean flag alongside the existing `bank` flag, threading it through parsing, quarter_figures, and headline computation so that revenue, EBITDA/PPOP, and NII are calculated correctly for NBFC filings while keeping bank logic untouched. def _segments(symbol: str) -> dict:
    """Latest quarter whose exchange XBRL filing carries a segment-revenue note (walks back up to 4 quarters)."""
    try:
        filings = nse.integrated_filings(symbol)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {}
    for qe in list(dict.fromkeys(f["qe"] for f in filings))[:4]:
        cur = nse.quarter_figures(symbol, qe, filings=filings)
        if cur and cur.get("segments"):
            break
    else:
        return {}
    latest = date.fromisoformat(qe)
    yoy = nse.quarter_figures(symbol, yoy_qe(latest).isoformat(), prefer=cur["basis"], filings=filings)
    prev_map = {s["name"].lower(): s["revenue"] for s in (yoy or {}).get("segments", [])}
    total = sum(s["revenue"] for s in cur["segments"] if s["revenue"] > 0) or 1
    segs = [{"name": s["name"], "revenue": s["revenue"], "share": s["revenue"] / total * 100,
             "yoy": pct_change(s["revenue"], prev_map.get(s["name"].lower()))} for s in cur["segments"]]
    segs.sort(key=lambda s: -s["revenue"])
    return {"quarter": fy_quarter_label(latest), "basis": cur["basis"], "items": segs,
            "source": {"label": f"Exchange XBRL segment note, {fy_quarter_label(latest)}", "url": cur["source"]["url"]}}

Actually I realize there's a bug in the name regex: compiling with the IGNORECASE flag means the capitalized-letter pattern also matches lowercase words, so a phrase like "as Chief" could get pulled into the captured name incorrectly. The regex engine's backtracking saves it in simple cases, but it's fragile elsewhere, so I should avoid applying case-insensitivity globally. Instead, I'll compile the pattern without re.I and use inline flag groups `(?i:...)` just around the keyword/honorific portions, keeping the name-matching segment strictly case-sensitive. 💭 #356 Reasoning 93m 58s
I'm finding that flash models with reasoning_effort set to none are noticeably faster and still accurate for extraction, while flash-lite models are slower and reject that setting entirely, and 503 errors seem to pop up intermittently across some of these models. The interesting design insight here is that "fast tier" doesn't require flash-lite — flash with thinking disabled is actually faster and cheaper since there are no thinking tokens, so I can treat reasoning effort as a dial: off for cheap extraction, low/medium for smarter judgment tasks, all within the same model family plus a fallback chain. Given cost and latency tradeoffs (flash-lite cheaper per token on paid tiers, free tier costing nothing, but flash being faster for UX), I'm sketching out a fast-tier chain and a smart-tier chain of models ordered by effort level, though rather than hardcoding specific model names I'd rather generate these chains automatically from the available models list using heuristics and health tracking. I'm working out the heuristics now: for candidates, sort stable flash models by version descending, then preview flash, then lite models; for the fast tier, prefer effort="none" and fall back to no param if a model rejects it with a 400; for the smart tier, use effort="low" or default. I also need a circuit-breaker scheme — mark a model unhealthy for 5 minutes on 503/429/timeout, dead for the process lifetime on 404, and move immediately to the next candidate. The tricky part is that newest models (3.8, 3.7) tend to be overloaded or slow to timeout, so they'd keep getting tried first and wasting time before health marking kicks in — I'm considering a startup warmup probe or ordering by known reliability to avoid that first costly failure. Instead of arbitrary version-based ordering, I think a better approach is to run a background startup probe — sending tiny requests to each candidate with a short timeout, measuring latency and health, then ordering chains by measured speed with healthy models first, and re-probing periodically. This makes the routing adaptive to model churn rather than relying on hardcoded assumptions, and the cost of these small probe calls is negligible against free-tier rate limits. I'm also considering simplifying this with explicit environment variable overrides for fast/smart models alongside the automatic chains, while leaving the main .env untouched. Now I'm sketching the actual LLM class structure to hold these probed chains. Writing model discovery logic... Still defining the chain logic... On error handling: 400s for unsupported params trigger a retry without that param, 404s mark the model dead, rate limits and server errors mark it unhealthy temporarily (longer for quota exhaustion), auth failures abort entirely, and after the whole chain fails I give it one more ignoring-health pass before giving up. I'm also weighing whether to probe models at startup, since relying purely on fallback could mean the very first request hits a slow model and eats a long timeout. I think running the probe in a background thread so the chain falls back on version ranking until probe results are ready is the way to go -- I'll build a warmup() function triggered at app startup. I also need to track which model actually served a response for usage logging, and rethink the cache key strategy: instead of keying by model name, it should key by tier plus prompt content so results can be reused across model switches, with the serving model stored separately. That means updating analyst.py's cache key logic too, since it currently pulls the model name directly rather than using a stable tier identifier. Now I'm ready to rewrite llm.py with these changes. Flash with reasoning off is fastest and accurate, flash-lite is slower and rejects that parameter, and the newest models are intermittently overloaded. I'll rework the router to use fallback chains per tier (fast: flash no-thinking, smart: flash low-thinking), ordered by a startup latency probe, with automatic failover and temporary blacklisting on errors like 503/429/timeout.

        store.set("llm", key, {"result": result, "_model": model})
        return result

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- actuals table
def _fmt(v, pct: bool = False, dec: int = 0) -> str:
    if v is None:
        return "n/a"
    return f"{v:+.1f}%" if pct else f"{v:,.{dec}f}"


def _actuals(d: dict) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
    rows = []
    for q in d["trajectory"]["quarters"]:
        try:
            qd = datetime.strptime(q["p"], "%b %Y").date()
            label = fy_quarter_label(qd.replace(day=30 if qd.month in (6, 9) else 31))
        except ValueError:
            label = q["p"]
        rows.append({"label": label, **q})
    lines = ["Quarter | Revenue (Rs Cr) | Rev YoY | Op. margin % | PAT (Rs Cr) | PAT YoY"]
    for r in rows:
        lines.append(f"{r['label']} | {_fmt(r['sales'])} | {_fmt(r['salesYoY'], True)} | {_fmt(r['opm'], dec=1)} | "
                     f"{_fmt(r['pat'])} | {_fmt(r['patYoY'], True)}")
    t = d["trajectory"]
    lines += ["", "Fiscal year | Revenue (Rs Cr) | Rev YoY | Op. margin % | PAT (Rs Cr)"]
    start = max(0, len(t["years"]) - 5)
    for idx in range(start, len(t["years"])):
        y = t["years"][idx]
        cur = t["sales"][idx]
        prev = t["sales"][idx - 1] if idx > 0 else None
        yoy = (cur / prev - 1) * 100 if cur and prev else None
        opm = t["opm"][idx] if idx < len(t["opm"]) else None
        pat = t["pat"][idx] if idx < len(t["pat"]) else None
        fy = f"FY{y[-2:]}" if y[-2:].isdigit() else y
        lines.append(f"{fy} (year to {y}) | {_fmt(cur)} | {_fmt(yoy, True)} | {_fmt(opm, dec=1)} | {_fmt(pat)}")
    return "\n".join(lines), rows


SYSTEM_JUDGE = ("You audit management credibility for a portfolio manager. Judge each guidance item ONLY with evidence provided: "
                "management's own reported numbers on LATER calls, or the financial actuals table. No outside knowledge. "
                "Evidence must post-date the call where the guidance was given. Output JSON only.")

PROMPT_JUDGE = """Company: {name}. Latest reported quarter in the table: {latest}. Calls in order (oldest first): {calls}.

GUIDANCE (id | given on call | horizon | target | statement):
{guidance}

LATER EVIDENCE - what management reported on each call (id | call | statement):
{reported}

FINANCIAL ACTUALS (company filings, standardised; YoY precomputed - do not recompute):
{actuals}

Rules:
- delivered / partly / missed only if the horizon has passed (or the evidence already settles it) AND you can cite evidence.
- pending if the horizon has not ended and nothing settles it yet. unverifiable if the horizon passed but no evidence covers it.
- "actual" must name the evidence: a reported id (e.g. T1-R2) or a table row (e.g. "Q4 FY26 row").

Return JSON:
{{"ledger": [{{"id": "<guidance id>", "verdict": "delivered|partly|missed|pending|unverifiable",
              "actual": "<=20 words: the specific actual number(s) and evidence id/row", "reason": "<=15 words"}}],
 "pattern": "over-delivers|reliable|mixed|over-promises|too early to tell",
 "summary": "<=2 sentences on management's track record: do they under-promise, miss, or move goalposts?"}}"""


def promises(symbol: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    key = f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}"
    cached = store.get("promises", key, max_age=12 * 3600)
    if cached:
        return cached
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"symbol": sym, "error": "No fundamentals found for this ticker"}
    ts = transcripts(sym, 4)
    if not ts:
        return {"symbol": sym, "calls": [], "items": [], "claims": [], "message": "No readable concall transcripts found."}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        extracted = list(ex.map(lambda t: _extract_one(d["name"], t), ts))
    items = [g for e in extracted for g in e["guidance"]]
    claims = [c for e in extracted for c in e["claims"]]
    reported = [r for e in extracted for r in e.get("reported", [])]
    actuals_text, _ = _actuals(d)
    latest = d["trajectory"]["quarters"][-1]["p"] if d["trajectory"]["quarters"] else "n/a"
    ledger, summary, pattern, judged_by = {}, None, None, None
    judgeable = [g for g in items if g.get("horizon") or g.get("target")]
    if llm.enabled and judgeable:
        gl = "\n".join(f"{g['id']} | {g['callQuarter']} call ({g['callPeriod']}) | {g.get('horizon') or '-'} | "
                       f"{g.get('target') or '-'} | {g['statement']}" for g in judgeable)
        rl = "\n".join(f"{r['id']} | {r['callQuarter']} call | {r['statement']}" for r in reported) or "none"
        order = ", ".join(f"{e['id']}={e['quarter']} ({e['period']})" for e in reversed(extracted))
        res = llm.json("smart", SYSTEM_JUDGE, PROMPT_JUDGE.format(name=d["name"], latest=latest, calls=order, guidance=gl,
                                                                  reported=rl, actuals=actuals_text),
                       purpose="promise_vs_delivery", max_tokens=8000)
        if isinstance(res, dict):
            ledger = {x["id"]: x for x in res.get("ledger") or [] if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("id")}
            summary, pattern, judged_by = res.get("summary"), res.get("pattern"), "llm"
    for g in items:
        j = ledger.get(g["id"])
        g["verdict"] = (j or {}).get("verdict") or ("unjudged" if not llm.enabled else "unverifiable")
        g["actual"] = (j or {}).get("actual")
        g["reason"] = (j or {}).get("reason")
    counts = Counter(g["verdict"] for g in items)
    judged = counts["delivered"] + counts["partly"] + counts["missed"]
    score = round((counts["delivered"] + 0.5 * counts["partly"]) / judged * 100) if judged >= 3 else None
    out = {
        "symbol": sym, "name": d["name"],
        "calls": [{k: e[k] for k in ("id", "period", "quarter", "url", "pages", "tone", "toneReason", "method")} |
                  {"guidance": len(e["guidance"]), "claims": len(e["claims"]), "reported": len(e.get("reported", [])),
                   "dropped": e.get("dropped", 0)} for e in extracted],
        "items": items, "claims": claims, "reported": reported,
        "score": {"credibility": score, "counts": dict(counts), "judged": judged},
        "pattern": pattern, "summary": summary,
        "method": {"extract": extracted[0]["method"] if extracted else None, "judge": judged_by,
                   "models": llm.models() if llm.enabled else None},
        "actualsTable": actuals_text,
    }
    store.set("promises", key, out)
    return out

"""Pull: the analyst layer on top of the deterministic dossier.

Grounding discipline (primary sources only):
  * Transcripts come straight from the exchange/company (links listed by screener.in).
  * The LLM only sees excerpts we select + numbers we computed; it must quote verbatim and cite
    page numbers / fact ids. We verify quotes against the transcript and drop anything uncited.
Model routing:
  * fast tier  -> per-transcript extraction (bulk reading, 4 calls)
  * smart tier -> promise-vs-delivery judgement and bull/bear synthesis (small, dense prompts)
  * no key     -> extractive fallbacks (quote mining + rules), clearly labelled.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import math
import re
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import date, datetime

from ..llm import llm
from ..sources import screener
from ..sources.pdftext import document_pages, has_text
from ..store import store
from ..util import clip, fy_quarter_label
from .research import dossier
from .results import latest_qe_before

log = logging.getLogger("finn.analyst")

PROMPT_VERSION = "v5"
_FWD = re.compile(r"\b(guid\w*|expect\w*|outlook|target\w*|aim\w*|aspir\w*|plan(?:s|ning)? to|going forward|next (?:year|quarter|fiscal|few)|"
                  r"fy ?'?2\d|fy ?\d\d|h[12]\b|by (?:the )?end of|over the next|we will|we should|should be|would be|likely to|"
                  r"anticipat\w*|estimat\w*|visibility|pipeline|capex|capacity|commission\w*|ramp[- ]?up|double)\b", re.I)
_NUM = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s?(?:%|percent|per cent|crore|crores|cr\b|bps|basis points|x\b|billion|million|lakh|mw|gw|units|tonnes|mtpa)", re.I)
_PAST = re.compile(r"\b(we (?:delivered|achieved|reported|grew|posted|clocked)|grew|declined|this quarter|during the quarter|year[- ]on[- ]year)\b", re.I)


def _norm(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", (s or "").lower()).strip()


def call_quarter(c: dict) -> str:
    d = date.fromisoformat(c["date"]) if c.get("date") else None
    return fy_quarter_label(latest_qe_before(d)) if d else c.get("period", "")


def transcripts(symbol: str, n: int = 4) -> list[dict]:
    s = screener.company(symbol)
    if not s:
        return []
    out = []
    for c in s["concalls"]:
        if not c.get("transcript"):
            continue
        pages = document_pages(c["transcript"])
        if not has_text(pages):
            continue
        out.append({"id": f"T{len(out) + 1}", "period": c["period"], "date": c.get("date"), "quarter": call_quarter(c),
                    "url": c["transcript"], "pages": pages})
        if len(out) >= n:
            break
    return out


def _paragraphs(t: dict) -> list[dict]:
    paras = []
    for pno, text in enumerate(t["pages"], start=1):
        for chunk in re.split(r"\n\s*\n|\n(?=[A-Z][A-Za-z\.\s]{2,40}:)", text):
            c = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", chunk).strip()
            if len(c) > 60:
                paras.append({"t": t["id"], "page": pno, "text": c})
    return paras


def _candidates(t: dict, budget: int = 11000) -> str:
    scored = []
    for p in _paragraphs(t):
        score = 2 * len(_FWD.findall(p["text"])) + 2 * len(_NUM.findall(p["text"])) + len(_PAST.findall(p["text"]))
        if score >= 3 and not re.match(r"(moderator|operator)\s*:", p["text"], re.I):
            scored.append((score, p))
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
    picked, used = [], 0
    for _, p in scored:
        if used + len(p["text"]) > budget:
            continue
        picked.append(p)
        used += len(p["text"])
    picked.sort(key=lambda p: p["page"])
    return "\n".join(f"[p.{p['page']}] {p['text']}" for p in picked)


def _verify_quote(quote: str, full_norm: str) -> bool:
    q = _norm(quote)
    if len(q) < 12:
        return False
    if q in full_norm:
        return True
    words = q.split()
    # tolerate small transcription differences: require two 6-word shingles to match
    shingles = [" ".join(words[i:i + 6]) for i in range(0, max(1, len(words) - 5), 3)]
    return sum(1 for s in shingles if s in full_norm) >= min(2, len(shingles))

Excerpts:
{text}"""


def _extract_one(name: str, t: dict) -> dict:
    full_norm = _norm(" ".join(t["pages"]))
    excerpt = _candidates(t)
    out = {"id": t["id"], "period": t["period"], "quarter": t["quarter"], "url": t["url"], "pages": len(t["pages"]),
           "guidance": [], "claims": [], "reported": [], "tone": None, "toneReason": None, "method": "extractive"}
    res = None
    if llm.enabled and excerpt:
        res = llm.json("fast", SYSTEM_EXTRACT, PROMPT_EXTRACT.format(name=name, period=t["period"], quarter=t["quarter"],
                                                                       text=excerpt), purpose="transcript_extract", max_tokens=4000)
    if isinstance(res, dict):
        out["method"] = "llm"
        for i, g in enumerate(res.get("guidance") or []):
            if isinstance(g, dict) and g.get("quote") and _verify_quote(g["quote"], full_norm):
                out["guidance"].append({**g, "id": f"{t['id']}-G{i + 1}", "call": t["id"], "callQuarter": t["quarter"],
                                        "callPeriod": t["period"], "url": t["url"]})
        for i, r in enumerate(res.get("reported") or []):
            if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("quote") and _verify_quote(r["quote"], full_norm):
                out["reported"].append({**r, "id": f"{t['id']}-R{i + 1}", "call": t["id"], "callQuarter": t["quarter"],
                                        "callPeriod": t["period"], "url": t["url"]})
        for i, c in enumerate(res.get("claims") or []):
            if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("quote") and _verify_quote(c["quote"], full_norm):
                out["claims"].append({**c, "id": f"{t['id']}-C{i + 1}", "call": t["id"], "callQuarter": t["quarter"], "url": t["url"]})
        out["tone"], out["toneReason"] = res.get("tone"), res.get("tone_reason")
        total = sum(len(res.get(k) or []) for k in ("guidance", "reported", "claims"))
        out["dropped"] = total - len(out["guidance"]) - len(out["claims"]) - len(out["reported"])
    else:
        # Extractive fallback: highest-signal forward-looking sentences, verbatim.
        sents = []
        for p in _paragraphs(t):
            for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", p["text"]):
                if (50 < len(s) < 320 and _FWD.search(s) and _NUM.search(s) and not s.rstrip().endswith("?")
                        and not re.match(r"(moderator|operator)", s, re.I)):

Then I need to compare each horizon end date against the latest reported quarter end to classify items as "ended," "open," or "unclear," accounting for reporting lag between fiscal year close and actual data availability. Finally, I'm deciding which items to pass to the judge—only those with ended or unparseable horizons—while considering whether open items with interim progress should also be included for an "on track/off track" assessment. Since the model's training cutoff might predate the actual present date, I need to explicitly state "today is 28 Oct 2026" and pre-compute status deterministically, so it doesn't have to reason about dates itself. I'm also planning to add a YTD aggregate row (Q1+Q2 FY27 summed with YoY comparisons) to the actuals table, since that's cheap to compute and useful for judging whether open guidance is on track. Rather than sending all 18-23 items to the judge in one giant call, I'll send just ended + open items — still sizeable but manageable, maybe 800 tokens of output. I noticed the smart model chain fell back to flash-lite in one run, taking 26.7s, likely because the preferred quick models were temporarily unavailable — not a major concern. The judge needs to cite evidence for "partly met" verdicts, and if a judge call fails and returns None, I should mark those items as "unjudged" rather than "unverifiable" to keep the distinction clear. I also want to de-duplicate guidance items before judging. Repeated guidance across calls (like the same revenue growth figure reiterated on consecutive quarters) is actually useful signal rather than clutter — it shows consistency or, if the numbers shift, a goalpost move worth flagging, which the summary prompt already asks about. So I'll skip deduping and just let the judge surface these patterns naturally. Now I'm moving on to building the horizon parser that handles strings like "FY27," "Q3 FY27," and "H2 FY27" coming from the LLM output. Writing regex patterns... Now I'm mapping fiscal quarter and half-year boundaries to actual calendar dates, like Q1 FY27 ending June 30 2026 and H1 FY27 ending in September. I'm also working out how to handle ranges like "FY27-28" or "FY27-FY28," taking the latest year as the target, and extending the regex to catch the second year after the dash. For relative phrases like "next 2-3 years" or "next year," I'm figuring out how to compute the resulting fiscal year from the call date, taking the maximum when a range is given. For "this year," I'm resolving it to the fiscal year containing the call date itself, noting ambiguity around quarter boundaries—e.g., a Q4 FY26 call held in May 2026 likely means "this year" refers to FY27 since FY26 has essentially closed out. def now_ist() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(IST)


def fy_quarter_label(d: date) -> str:
    """Quarter-end date -> Indian fiscal label, e.g. 2026-09-30 -> 'Q2 FY27'."""
    q = {6: 1, 9: 2, 12: 3, 3: 4}.get(d.month)
    fy = d.year + 1 if d.month >= 4 else d.year
    return f"Q{q} FY{fy % 100:02d}" if q else d.strftime("%b %Y")

def _facts(d: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    facts = []
    add = lambda text: facts.append((f"F{len(facts) + 1}", text))  # noqa: E731
    sn = d["snapshot"]
    if sn.get("marketCap"):
        add(f"Market cap Rs {sn['marketCap']:,.0f} Cr; P/E {sn.get('pe') or 'n/a'}; ROCE {sn.get('roce') or 'n/a'}%; ROE {sn.get('roe') or 'n/a'}%")
    if sn.get("ttmRevenue"):
        add(f"TTM revenue Rs {sn['ttmRevenue']:,.0f} Cr, TTM PAT Rs {(sn.get('ttmPat') or 0):,.0f} Cr, TTM operating margin {sn.get('ttmOpm') or 0:.1f}%")
    for s in d["trajectory"]["signals"] + d["balance"]["signals"] + d["cash"]["signals"] + d["holding"]["signals"]:
        add(s)
    seg = d.get("segments") or {}
    if seg.get("items"):
        parts = ", ".join(f"{x['name']} {x['share']:.0f}%" + (f" ({x['yoy']:+.0f}% YoY)" if x.get("yoy") is not None else "")
                          for x in seg["items"][:6])
        add(f"Segment revenue mix {seg['quarter']}: {parts}")
    for q in d["trajectory"]["quarters"][-4:]:
        if q["sales"] is not None:
            add(f"{q['p']} quarter: revenue Rs {q['sales']:,.0f} Cr ({_fmt(q['salesYoY'], True)} YoY), "
                f"op. margin {_fmt(q['opm'], dec=1)}%, PAT Rs {_fmt(q['pat'])} Cr ({_fmt(q['patYoY'], True)} YoY)")
    return facts


def thesis(symbol: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    key = f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}"
    cached = store.get("thesis", key, max_age=12 * 3600)
    if cached:
        return cached
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"symbol": sym, "error": "No fundamentals found for this ticker"}
    facts = _facts(d)
    p = promises(sym) if d else {}
    claims = [(f"C{i + 1}", c) for i, c in enumerate((p.get("claims") or [])[:10])]
    track = (f"{p['score']['credibility']}% of judged guidance delivered ({p['score']['judged']} judged); pattern: {p.get('pattern')}"
             if p.get("score", {}).get("credibility") is not None else "not enough judged guidance")
    out = {"symbol": sym, "facts": [{"id": i, "text": t} for i, t in facts],
           "claims": [{"id": i, "text": c.get("claim"), "quote": c.get("quote"), "page": c.get("page"), "call": c.get("callQuarter"),
                       "url": c.get("url")} for i, c in claims],
           "narrative": [], "bull": [], "bear": [], "watch": [], "oneLiner": None, "method": "rules"}
    valid = {i for i, _ in facts} | {i for i, _ in claims}
    if llm.enabled:
        res = llm.json("smart", SYSTEM_THESIS, PROMPT_THESIS.format(
            name=d["name"], facts="\n".join(f"{i}: {t}" for i, t in facts),
            claims="\n".join(f"{i} ({c.get('callQuarter')} call, p.{c.get('page')}): \"{c.get('quote')}\"" for i, c in claims) or "none",
            track=track), purpose="thesis", max_tokens=3000, temperature=0.2)
        if isinstance(res, dict):
            def keep(items):
                good = []
                for it in items or []:
                    if isinstance(it, dict):
                        refs = [r for r in it.get("refs") or [] if r in valid]
                        if refs:
                            good.append({**it, "refs": refs})
                return good
            out.update(narrative=keep(res.get("narrative")), bull=keep(res.get("bull")), bear=keep(res.get("bear")),
                       watch=res.get("watch") or [], oneLiner=res.get("oneLiner"), method="llm")
    if out["method"] == "rules":
        # Deterministic fallback: sort computed facts into supportive vs worrying by keywords.
        for fid, t in facts:
            low = t.lower()
            if any(k in low for k in ("pressure", "not showing up", "lengthening", "jumped", "highly geared",
                                      "compressing", "holding down", "lagged")):
                out["bear"].append({"point": t, "refs": [fid]})
            elif any(k in low for k in ("operating leverage", "turning into cash", "improving", "lightly geared",
                                        "compounded", "expanding", "holding up")):
                out["bull"].append({"point": t, "refs": [fid]})
    store.set("thesis", key, out)
    return out


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ask (BM25 + LLM)
_TOK = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")
_STOP = set("the a an and or of to in on for is are was were be been it this that with as at by from we our you they their its has have had will would can could should what did does do about how why which".split())
_SYN = {
    "smartphone": ["mobile", "phone", "phones", "handset", "smartphones"], "smartphones": ["mobile", "phone", "phones", "handset"],
    "mobile": ["smartphone", "phone", "handset"], "phones": ["mobile", "smartphone", "handset"],
    "margin": ["margins", "ebitda", "profitability", "opm"], "margins": ["margin", "ebitda", "profitability"],
    "revenue": ["sales", "topline", "turnover", "revenues"], "growth": ["grow", "growing", "increase"],
    "capex": ["capital", "investment", "capacity", "plant", "expansion"], "debt": ["borrowing", "borrowings", "leverage"],
    "guidance": ["expect", "target", "outlook", "guide"], "volume": ["volumes", "units", "million"],
    "volumes": ["volume", "units", "million"], "demand": ["consumption", "orders", "offtake"],
    "fy27": ["fy", "27", "2027", "year"], "fy26": ["fy", "26", "2026", "year"], "fy28": ["fy", "28", "2028"],
}


def _tokens(s: str) -> list[str]:
    return [w for w in _TOK.findall(s.lower()) if w not in _STOP and len(w) > 1]


def _expand(q: str) -> str:
    toks = _tokens(q)
    return " ".join(toks + [s for t in toks for s in _SYN.get(t, [])])


def _chunks(t: dict, words: int = 90) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for pno, text in enumerate(t["pages"], start=1):
        sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text))
        buf: list[str] = []
        for s in sents:
            buf.append(s)
            if sum(len(x.split()) for x in buf) >= words:
                out.append({"page": pno, "text": " ".join(buf)})
                buf = buf[-1:]
        if buf and sum(len(x.split()) for x in buf) > 15:
            out.append({"page": pno, "text": " ".join(buf)})
    return out


def _bm25(query: str, docs: list[dict], k: int = 8) -> list[dict]:
    q = _tokens(query)
    toks = [_tokens(d["text"]) for d in docs]
    n = len(docs)
    avg = sum(len(t) for t in toks) / max(1, n)
    df = Counter(w for t in toks for w in set(t))
    scored = []
    for d, t in zip(docs, toks):
        tf = Counter(t)
        s = 0.0
        for w in q:
            if w in tf:
                idf = math.log(1 + (n - df[w] + 0.5) / (df[w] + 0.5))
                s += idf * tf[w] * 2.2 / (tf[w] + 1.2 * (0.25 + 0.75 * len(t) / avg))
        if s > 0:
            scored.append((s * d.get("boost", 1.0), d))
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
    return [d for _, d in scored[:k]]


SYSTEM_ASK = ("You answer a portfolio manager's question using ONLY the numbered sources (earnings-call transcripts and "
              "numbers computed from filings). Cite like [T1 p.4] or [F3] after each claim. If the sources don't contain "
              "the answer, say exactly what is missing. <=120 words. Output JSON only.")


def ask(symbol: str, question: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"answer": "I couldn't find fundamentals for this ticker.", "sources": []}
    docs = []
    for t in transcripts(sym, 4):
        for c in _chunks(t):
            docs.append({"id": f"{t['id']} p.{c['page']}", "label": f"{t['quarter']} call transcript, p.{c['page']}",
                         "url": t["url"], "text": c["text"]})
    # Structured guidance / reported numbers already extracted are dense, high-signal documents.
    cached_p = store.get("promises", f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}")
    for g in (cached_p or {}).get("items", []) + (cached_p or {}).get("reported", []):
        page = g.get("page")
        docs.append({"id": f"{g['call']} p.{page}" if page else g["call"], "label": f"{g['callQuarter']} call" + (f", p.{page}" if page else ""),
                     "url": g["url"], "text": f"{g['statement']} {g.get('target') or ''} {g.get('horizon') or ''}. \"{g['quote']}\"", "boost": 1.4})
    facts = _facts(d)
    for fid, text in facts:
        docs.append({"id": fid, "label": "Computed from filings", "url": None, "text": text})
    hits = _bm25(_expand(question), docs, 10)
    seen, uniq = set(), []
    for h in hits:
        if (h["id"], h["text"][:60]) not in seen:
            seen.add((h["id"], h["text"][:60]))
            uniq.append(h)

def _parse_json(text: str) -> Any:
    text = text.strip()
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\s*", "", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\s*```\s*$", "", text)
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        starts = [i for i in (text.find("{"), text.find("[")) if i >= 0]
        if not starts:
            raise
        # Parse the first complete JSON value and ignore any trailing chatter.
        value, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[min(starts):])
        return value

def pct_change(new: float | None, old: float | None) -> float | None:
    if new is None or old is None or old == 0:
        return None
    return (new - old) / abs(old) * 100.0


def cagr(end: float | None, start: float | None, years: float) -> float | None:
    if end is None or start is None or start <= 0 or end <= 0 or years <= 0:
        return None
    return ((end / start) ** (1 / years) - 1) * 100.0

"""Shared HTTP client: polite per-host pacing, retries, response caching and
stale-on-error fallback so the demo keeps working when a source blocks us."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import logging
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx

from .config import FILES_DIR, OFFLINE, USER_AGENT
from .store import store

log = logging.getLogger("finn.http")

# Minimum seconds between requests to the same host (be a good citizen).
HOST_INTERVAL = {
    "www.nseindia.com": 0.35,
    "www.screener.in": 1.2,
    "query1.finance.yahoo.com": 0.15,
}


class FetchError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Http:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.client = httpx.Client(
            headers={
                "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
                "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
            },
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(45.0, connect=15.0),
            follow_redirects=True,
✔ #471 view - view the file at Q:\sp\finn\backend\app\http.py. 123m 41s
Q:\sp\finn\backend\app\http.py (lines 40-60)
            follow_redirects=True,
        )
        self._host_locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = {}
        self._last_call: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._meta_lock = threading.Lock()

    def _pace(self, host: str) -> threading.Lock:
        with self._meta_lock:
            return self._host_locks.setdefault(host, threading.Lock())

    def get(self, url: str, headers: dict | None = None, retries: int = 3) -> httpx.Response:
        if OFFLINE:
            raise FetchError("offline mode")
        host = urlparse(url).netloc
        interval = HOST_INTERVAL.get(host, 0.0)
        last_exc: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(retries):
            with self._pace(host):
                wait = self._last_call.get(host, 0) + interval - time.time()
                if wait > 0:
                    time.sleep(wait)

def promises(symbol: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    key = f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}"
    cached = store.get("promises", key, max_age=12 * 3600)
    if cached:
        return cached
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"symbol": sym, "error": "No fundamentals found for this ticker"}
    ts = transcripts(sym, 6)  # ~18 months of calls, so annual guidance has time to come due
    if not ts:
        return {"symbol": sym, "calls": [], "items": [], "claims": [], "message": "No readable concall transcripts found."}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(3) as ex:
        extracted = list(ex.map(lambda t: _extract_one(d["name"], t), ts))
    items = [g for e in extracted for g in e["guidance"]]
    claims = [c for e in extracted for c in e["claims"]]
    reported = [r for e in extracted for r in e.get("reported", [])]
    actuals_text, _ = _actuals(d)
    latest = d["trajectory"]["quarters"][-1]["p"] if d["trajectory"]["quarters"] else "n/a"
    ev_end = _evidence_end(d, extracted)
    for g in items:
        end = horizon_end(g.get("horizon"), _iso(g.get("callDate")))
        g["horizonEnd"] = end.isoformat() if end else None
        g["status"] = "closed" if end and ev_end and end <= ev_end else "open"

    ledger, summary, pattern, judged_by = None, None, None, None
    if llm.enabled and items:
        row = lambda g: (f"{g['id']} | {g['callQuarter']} call ({g['callPeriod']}) | {g.get('horizon') or '-'} | "  # noqa: E731
                         f"{g.get('target') or '-'} | {g['statement']}")
        closed = [row(g) for g in items if g["status"] == "closed"]
        open_ = [row(g) for g in items if g["status"] == "open"]
        res = llm.json("smart", SYSTEM_JUDGE, PROMPT_JUDGE.format(
            name=d["name"], today=date.today().strftime("%d %b %Y"), latest=latest,
            ev_end=ev_end.strftime("%d %b %Y") if ev_end else "n/a",

    }

class LLM:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=15.0))
        self._sem = threading.Semaphore(config.LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._ids: list[str] | None = None
        self._health: dict[str, dict] = {}   # model -> {until, dead, lat, no_effort}
        self._probed_at = 0.0
        self.last_error: str | None = None

    # ---- configuration -------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(config.LLM_API_KEY)

    def _headers(self) -> dict:
        return {"Authorization": f"******", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

    def _model_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        if self._ids is not None:
            return self._ids
        ids = store.get("llm_models", config.LLM_BASE_URL, max_age=86400)
        if ids is None:
            try:
                r = self._client.get(config.LLM_BASE_URL + "models", headers=self._headers(), timeout=20)
                r.raise_for_status()
                ids = [m["id"].removeprefix("models/") for m in r.json().get("data", [])]
                store.set("llm_models", config.LLM_BASE_URL, ids)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                self.last_error = f"model discovery failed: {e}"
                log.warning(self.last_error)
                ids = []
        self._ids = ids
        return ids

    def _ok(self, mid: str) -> bool:
        h = self._health.get(mid, {})
        return not h.get("dead") and h.get("until", 0) < time.time()

    def chain(self, tier: str) -> list[str]:
        """Ordered candidates for a tier: overrides first, then healthy models (fast: by latency,
        smart: by quality), then everything else as a last resort."""
        override = config.LLM_MODEL_FAST if tier == "fast" else config.LLM_MODEL_SMART
        cands = text_models(self._model_ids())
        if not cands and override:
            return [override]
        full = [m for m in cands if "lite" not in m.lower()]
        lite = [m for m in cands if "lite" in m.lower()]
        lat = lambda m: self._health.get(m, {}).get("lat", 999.0)  # noqa: E731
        if tier == "fast":
            # extraction: fastest measured model first (unmeasured ones fall back to newest-first)
            ordered = sorted(full, key=lambda m: (lat(m), -_version(m))) + sorted(lite, key=lat)
        else:
            # judgement: best quality among models that answered quickly, then the rest
            quick = [m for m in full if lat(m) <= 15]
            ordered = sorted(quick, key=_quality_rank, reverse=True) + \
                sorted([m for m in full if m not in quick], key=lambda m: (lat(m), -_version(m))) + sorted(lite, key=lat)
        if override:
            ordered = [override] + [m for m in ordered if m != override]
        healthy = [m for m in ordered if self._ok(m)]
        return healthy + [m for m in ordered if m not in healthy]

    def models(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        if not self.enabled:
            return {}
        return {"fast": (self.chain("fast") or ["?"])[0], "smart": (self.chain("smart") or ["?"])[0]}

    # ---- health probe ----------------------------------------------------------
    def warmup(self) -> None:
        """Measure latency of each candidate with a tiny request (background, ~10 tokens each)."""
        if not self.enabled or time.time() - self._probed_at < 3600:
            return
        self._probed_at = time.time()
        cands = text_models(self._model_ids())[:12]

        def probe(mid: str):
            body = {"model": mid, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}], "max_tokens": 16}
            if "lite" not in mid:
                body["reasoning_effort"] = "none"
            t = time.time()
            try:
                r = self._client.post(config.LLM_BASE_URL + "chat/completions", headers=self._headers(), json=body, timeout=20)
                self._record(mid, r.status_code, time.time() - t, r.text)
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                self._record(mid, 599, time.time() - t, "timeout")

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex:
            list(ex.map(probe, cands))
        log.info("LLM probe: %s", {m: (round(h.get("lat", 0), 1), "ok" if self._ok(m) else "down")
                                   for m, h in self._health.items()})

    def _record(self, mid: str, status: int, seconds: float, text: str = "") -> None:
        h = self._health.setdefault(mid, {})
        if status == 200:
            h["lat"] = seconds if "lat" not in h else 0.6 * h["lat"] + 0.4 * seconds
            h["until"] = 0
        elif status == 404:
            h["dead"] = True
        elif status == 400 and "reasoning" in text.lower():
            h["no_effort"] = True
        elif status in (429,):
            daily = re.search(r"per ?day|perday|daily", text, re.I) is not None
            h["until"] = time.time() + (3600 if daily else 65)
        elif status >= 500 or status == 599:
            h["until"] = time.time() + 240
            h["lat"] = 999.0 if status == 599 else max(h.get("lat", 0), 30.0)

    # ---- calls ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def json(self, tier: str, system: str, prompt: str, *, purpose: str, max_tokens: int = 4096,
             temperature: float = 0.1) -> Any | None:
        """Return parsed JSON from the model, or None if the LLM is unavailable/failed."""
        if not self.enabled:
            return None
        key = hashlib.sha256(f"{tier}\n{system}\n{prompt}".encode()).hexdigest()
        cached = store.get("llm", key)
        if cached is not None:
            self._meter(tier, cached.get("_model", "?") if isinstance(cached, dict) else "?", purpose, cached=True)
            return _unwrap(cached.get("result") if isinstance(cached, dict) and "result" in cached else cached)
        t0 = time.time()
        data, model = self._call(tier, system, prompt, max_tokens, temperature)
        if data is None:
            return None
        try:
            content = data["choices"][0]["message"].get("content") or ""
            result = _unwrap(_parse_json(content))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            self.last_error = f"unparseable LLM output for {purpose} ({model}): {e}"
            log.warning(self.last_error)
            return None
        self._meter(tier, model, purpose, cached=False, usage=data.get("usage") or {}, ms=int((time.time() - t0) * 1000))
        store.set("llm", key, {"result": result, "_model": model})
        return result

    def _call(self, tier: str, system: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int, temperature: float):
        url = config.LLM_BASE_URL + "chat/completions"
        for attempt in range(2):
            for mid in self.chain(tier):
                if attempt == 0 and not self._ok(mid):
                    continue
                h = self._health.get(mid, {})
                body: dict[str, Any] = {
                    "model": mid, "temperature": temperature, "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                    "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                    "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
                }
                if not h.get("no_effort") and "lite" not in mid:
                    body["reasoning_effort"] = EFFORT[tier]
                for _ in range(3):  # same model: only to strip unsupported params
                    t = time.time()
                    with self._sem:
                        try:
                            r = self._client.post(url, headers=self._headers(), json=body, timeout=TIMEOUT[tier])
                        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
                            self._record(mid, 599, time.time() - t)
                            self.last_error = f"{mid}: network/timeout ({e.__class__.__name__})"
                            break
                    if r.status_code == 200:
                        msg = (r.json().get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("message") or {}
                        if not msg.get("content"):  # thinking ate the budget: try next model
                            self.last_error = f"{mid}: empty completion"
                            break
                        self._record(mid, 200, time.time() - t)
                        self.last_error = None
                        return r.json(), mid
                    text = r.text[:400]
                    if r.status_code in (401, 403):
                        self.last_error = f"LLM auth failed ({r.status_code}) - check GEMINI_API_KEY"
                        log.error(self.last_error)
                        return None, None
                    if r.status_code == 400 and "reasoning_effort" in body:
                        self._health.setdefault(mid, {})["no_effort"] = True
                        body.pop("reasoning_effort")
                        continue
                    if r.status_code == 400 and "response_format" in body:
                        body.pop("response_format")
                        continue
                    self._record(mid, r.status_code, time.time() - t, text)
                    self.last_error = f"{mid}: HTTP {r.status_code}"
                    log.warning("LLM %s failed on %s (HTTP %s) - falling through", tier, mid, r.status_code)
                    break
            time.sleep(3)
        return None, None

    # ---- metering ------------------------------------------------------------
    def _meter(self, tier: str, model: str, purpose: str, *, cached: bool, usage: dict | None = None,
               ms: int = 0) -> None:
        usage = usage or {}

        def update(u: dict | None) -> dict:
            u = u or {"calls": 0, "cached": 0, "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "by_purpose": {}, "recent": []}
            p = u["by_purpose"].setdefault(purpose, {"calls": 0, "cached": 0, "tokens": 0, "tier": tier})
            if cached:
                u["cached"] += 1
                p["cached"] += 1
            else:
                u["calls"] += 1
                p["calls"] += 1
                u["input_tokens"] += usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
                u["output_tokens"] += usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)
                p["tokens"] += usage.get("total_tokens", 0)
            u["recent"] = ([{"t": time.time(), "tier": tier, "model": model, "purpose": purpose, "cached": cached,
                             "tokens": usage.get("total_tokens", 0), "ms": ms}] + u["recent"])[:40]
            return u

        store.update_state("llm_usage", update)

Likely cause: a prior heavy batch (multiple symbols times several extraction calls) hit per-model RPM limits on the free tier, which pushed those models into their 65-second cooldown window, so the lite models stepped in as fallback. That matches expectations for free-tier rate limits, so the fallthrough design is working as intended. Writing JSON validation logic... For the 200-status branch, I'm handling the response payload by extracting the message content, parsing it, and recording success or logging a parse failure before falling through to the next model in the chain. If every model fails, the call returns nothing to signal total failure upstream. On a parse failure specifically, I'm choosing not to record health since the model itself is still reachable — that distinction seems right. I should also check whether other places in the app call `_call` directly besides warmup, since those paths matter for consistency.

💭 #518 Reasoning 136m 2s
I'm updating the extraction prompt's scope wording to clarify when it should be "company" versus a specific segment or product name, which means the extraction cache will need to be invalidated again. I'm also writing a helper function to check whether a given scope string represents the company as a whole. For `_collapse` and `_settle`, I'm using that company check to decide whether to key by "company" or by a normalized segment name, and setting a `segment_scope` flag accordingly. Now I'm adding a numeric sanity check that looks for percentage values in the target and evidence to catch cases where a "higher is better" metric like margin or revenue growth falls clearly short of its percentage target, while being careful to skip targets that are phrased as upper bounds. Then I'm updating `_settle` to downgrade a verdict to "behind" or "partly" when this shortfall detection triggers and the original verdict was "delivered" or "on_track". I need to return both the shortfall value and the target low-end so I can compute a ratio for deciding "partly" versus "missed" — close to threshold counts as partly, further off counts as missed. I'm checking this logic against a few examples like revenue growth ranges and margin targets to make sure the thresholds feel consistent with how a judge would interpret "partly" versus "missed." I also want to make sure the comparisons stay like-for-like — skipping unrelated metrics (like capex percentages) and being cautious about comparing different margin types (EBITDA vs PAT) that shouldn't be conflated. For the number check, I'm stripping ticket IDs and fiscal year labels before checking if any digit remains in the actual text, so things like "T1-R4 / T2 evidence" with no real numbers get flagged as "No number cited," while something like "FY26 row Rev YoY: +4.9%" still passes since it retains a real digit after stripping the label. I also want to strengthen the judge prompt by adding a like-for-like rule requiring the cited number to measure the same metric as the target. After that I'll re-run extraction on all five names plus TRENT since the prompt wording changed, and use that time to start on the frontend PromiseTracker work before making the backend edits. I'll add a scope helper, a stricter "number cited" check, and a deterministic numeric sanity check—so cases like citing a ~10% margin target against an actual 7.2% can't be marked "on track."
