type Receipt = { title: string; quote?: string; text?: string; page?: number; url?: string | null; meta?: string };

function DossierView({ symbol, onBack }: { symbol: string; onBack: () => void }) {
  const [d, setD] = useState<Dossier | null>(null);
  const [err, setErr] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [p, setP] = useState<Promises | null>(null);
  const [t, setT] = useState<Thesis | null>(null);
  const [receipt, setReceipt] = useState<Receipt | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    api.dossier(symbol).then((x) => {
      setD(x);
      api.promises(symbol).then(setP).catch(() => setP({ symbol, calls: [], items: [], claims: [], message: "Couldn't read transcripts." }));
      api.thesis(symbol).then(setT).catch(() => {});
    }).catch((e) => setErr(String(e.message ?? e)));
  }, [symbol]);

  const refText = (id: string): Receipt | null => {
    const f = t?.facts.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (f) return { title: `Fact ${id}`, text: f.text, meta: "Computed from company filings" };
    const c = t?.claims.find((x) => x.id === id);
    if (c) return { title: `Management, ${c.call} call`, quote: c.quote, page: c.page, url: c.url };
    return null;
  };

  if (err) return (
    <div className="pb-28">
      <BackBar onBack={onBack} title={symbol} />
      <Empty icon={<CircleAlert size={26} />} title={`Couldn't research ${symbol}`} sub={err} />
    </div>
  );

  return (
    <div className="pb-28">
      <BackBar onBack={onBack} title={d?.name ?? symbol} />
      {!d ? (
        <div className="mt-3 space-y-3"><Skeleton className="h-28 w-full rounded-[20px]" /><Skeleton className="h-44 w-full rounded-[20px]" /><Skeleton className="h-44 w-full rounded-[20px]" /></div>
      ) : (
        <>
          <Header d={d} />
          <nav className="sticky top-[52px] z-20 -mx-4 mt-3 flex gap-1.5 overflow-x-auto bg-ink-950/85 px-4 py-2 backdrop-blur no-scrollbar">
            {NAV.map(([id, label]) => (
              <a key={id} href={`#${id}`} className="whitespace-nowrap rounded-full bg-white/[0.05] px-3 py-1.5 text-[12px] font-medium text-mute hover:text-white">{label}</a>
            ))}
          </nav>
          <Take t={t} p={p} onRef={(id) => setReceipt(refText(id))} />
          <PromiseTracker p={p} onReceipt={setReceipt} />
          <Narrative t={t} onRef={(id) => setReceipt(refText(id))} />
          <Business d={d} />
          <Numbers d={d} />
          <Balance d={d} />
          <Cash d={d} />
          <Owners d={d} />
          <Sources d={d} p={p} />
          <Ask symbol={symbol} onReceipt={setReceipt} />
        </>
      )}
      <Sheet open={!!receipt} onClose={() => setReceipt(null)} title={<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Quote size={16} className="text-fin" /> Receipt</span>}>
        {receipt && (
          <div className="space-y-3">
            <div className="text-[12px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-mute">{receipt.title}{receipt.page ? ` · page ${receipt.page}` : ""}</div>
            {receipt.quote && <blockquote className="rounded-xl border-l-2 border-fin bg-white/[0.03] p-3 text-[14px] leading-relaxed">“{receipt.quote}”</blockquote>}
            {receipt.text && <p className="text-[14px] leading-relaxed">{receipt.text}</p>}
            {receipt.meta && <p className="text-[12px] text-mute">{receipt.meta}</p>}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- take
function Take({ t, p, onRef }: { t: Thesis | null; p: Promises | null; onRef: (id: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <>
      <SectionTitle id="take">FINN's take</SectionTitle>
      {!t ? <Pending what="Weighing the numbers against what management said…" /> : (
        <div className="space-y-3">
          {t.oneLiner && (
            <div className="card border-fin/20 bg-fin/[0.05] p-4">
              <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[11px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-fin"><Sparkles size={13} /> The debate</div>
              <p className="mt-1.5 text-[15px] leading-snug">{t.oneLiner}</p>
              {p?.score?.credibility != null && <p className="mt-2 text-[12px] text-mute">Management kept {p.score.credibility}% of judged promises ({p.score.judged} judged).</p>}
            </div>
          )}
          <div className="grid gap-3">
            <CaseCard title="Bull case" icon={<TrendingUp size={15} />} color="text-up" items={t.bull} onRef={onRef} />
            <CaseCard title="Bear case" icon={<TrendingDown size={15} />} color="text-down" items={t.bear} onRef={onRef} />
          </div>
          {t.watch.length > 0 && (
            <div className="card p-4">
              <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-mute"><Target size={13} /> Watch next quarter</div>
              <ul className="mt-2 space-y-1.5 text-[13px]">{t.watch.map((w) => <li key={w} className="flex gap-2"><span className="mt-2 h-1 w-1 shrink-0 rounded-full bg-fin" />{w}</li>)}</ul>
            </div>
          )}
          {t.method !== "llm" && <p className="px-1 text-[11px] text-dim">Rule-based view (no LLM key configured): facts sorted into supportive vs. worrying.</p>}
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  );
}

function CaseCard({ title, icon, color, items, onRef }: { title: string; icon: React.ReactNode; color: string; items: { point: string; refs: string[] }[]; onRef: (id: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <div className="card p-4">
      <div className={cls("flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider", color)}>{icon} {title}</div>
      {items.length === 0 ? <p className="mt-2 text-[13px] text-mute">Nothing stood out.</p> : (
        <ul className="mt-2 space-y-2.5">
          {items.map((b, i) => (
            <li key={i} className="text-[13.5px] leading-snug">
              {b.point}
              <span className="ml-1 inline-flex flex-wrap gap-1 align-middle">
                {b.refs.map((r) => <button key={r} onClick={() => onRef(r)} className="rounded bg-white/[0.07] px-1.5 py-px text-[10px] font-semibold text-mute hover:bg-fin/20 hover:text-fin">{r}</button>)}
              </span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- promise tracker
function Gauge({ value }: { value: number }) {
  const r = 34, c = 2 * Math.PI * r;
  const color = value >= 70 ? "var(--color-up)" : value >= 45 ? "var(--color-warn)" : "var(--color-down)";
  return (
    <svg width="84" height="84" viewBox="0 0 84 84">
      <circle cx="42" cy="42" r={r} stroke="rgba(255,255,255,.07)" strokeWidth="8" fill="none" />
      <circle cx="42" cy="42" r={r} stroke={color} strokeWidth="8" fill="none" strokeLinecap="round"
        strokeDasharray={`${(value / 100) * c} ${c}`} transform="rotate(-90 42 42)" />
      <text x="42" y="47" textAnchor="middle" className="fill-white text-[17px] font-semibold num">{value}%</text>
    </svg>
  );
}

function PromiseTracker({ p, onReceipt }: { p: Promises | null; onReceipt: (r: Receipt) => void }) {
  const byCall = useMemo(() => {
    const m = new Map<string, Guidance[]>();
    p?.items.forEach((g) => m.set(g.callQuarter, [...(m.get(g.callQuarter) ?? []), g]));
    return [...m.entries()];
  }, [p]);
  return (
    <>
      <SectionTitle id="promises">Promised vs delivered</SectionTitle>
      {!p ? <Pending what="Reading the last four earnings-call transcripts…" /> : p.items.length === 0 ? (
        <Empty icon={<BookOpen size={24} />} title="No guidance found" sub={p.message ?? p.error ?? "Management didn't give measurable guidance in recent calls."} />
      ) : (
        <div className="space-y-3">
          <div className="card flex items-center gap-4 p-4">
            {p.score?.credibility != null ? <Gauge value={p.score.credibility} /> : (
              <div className="flex h-[84px] w-[84px] shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border-8 border-white/5 text-[11px] text-mute">no verdicts</div>
            )}
            <div className="min-w-0">
              <div className="text-[15px] font-semibold first-letter:uppercase">{p.pattern ?? "Guidance on record"}</div>
              <p className="mt-1 text-[13px] leading-snug text-mute">{p.summary ?? `${p.items.length} forward-looking statements from ${p.calls.length} calls. Add an LLM key to have FINN judge each against reported numbers.`}</p>
              {p.score && (
                <div className="mt-2 flex flex-wrap gap-1.5 text-[11px]">
                  {(["delivered", "partly", "missed", "pending"] as const).filter((k) => p.score!.counts[k]).map((k) => (
                    <span key={k} className={cls("rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 font-semibold", VERDICT[k].cls)}>{p.score!.counts[k]} {VERDICT[k].label.toLowerCase()}</span>
                  ))}
                </div>
              )}
            </div>
          </div>
          {byCall.map(([q, items]) => (
            <div key={q} className="card overflow-hidden">
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-b hairline bg-white/[0.02] px-4 py-2 text-[12px]">
                <span className="font-semibold">{q} earnings call</span>
                <span className="text-mute">{p.calls.find((c) => c.quarter === q)?.tone ?? ""}</span>
              </div>
              <ul className="divide-y divide-white/5">
                {items.map((g) => (
                  <li key={g.id}>
                    <button onClick={() => onReceipt({ title: `${g.callQuarter} call (${g.callPeriod})`, quote: g.quote, page: g.page, url: g.url,
                      meta: g.actual ? `Actual: ${g.actual}${g.reason ? ` — ${g.reason}` : ""}` : undefined })}
                      className="w-full px-4 py-3 text-left hover:bg-white/[0.02]">
                      <div className="flex items-start gap-2">
                        <p className="flex-1 text-[13.5px] leading-snug">{g.statement}</p>
                        <span className={cls("shrink-0 rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-[10.5px] font-semibold", VERDICT[g.verdict]?.cls)}>{VERDICT[g.verdict]?.label}</span>
                      </div>
                      <div className="mt-1 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 text-[11.5px] text-mute">
                        {g.target && <span>Target: <span className="text-white/80">{g.target}</span></span>}
                        {g.horizon && <span className="flex items-center gap-0.5"><Clock size={11} /> {g.horizon}</span>}
                        <span className="text-dim">p.{g.page}</span>
                      </div>
                      {g.actual && <div className="mt-1 text-[12px] text-white/75">→ {g.actual}</div>}
                    </button>
                  </li>
                ))}
              </ul>
            </div>
          ))}
          <p className="px-1 text-[11px] text-dim">
            {p.calls.reduce((a, c) => a + c.pages, 0)} transcript pages read · quotes verified against source
            {p.method?.models ? ` · extraction ${p.method.models.fast}, judgement ${p.method.models.smart}` : " · extractive mode"}
          </p>
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  );
}

function Narrative({ t, onRef }: { t: Thesis | null; onRef: (id: string) => void }) {
  if (!t || t.narrative.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <>
      <SectionTitle>Narrative vs numbers</SectionTitle>
      <div className="card divide-y divide-white/5">
        {t.narrative.map((n, i) => (
          <div key={i} className="p-4">
            <div className="flex items-start gap-2">
              <p className="flex-1 text-[13.5px] font-medium leading-snug">“{n.claim}”</p>
              <span className={cls("shrink-0 rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-[10.5px] font-semibold", VERDICT[n.verdict]?.cls ?? "bg-white/10 text-mute")}>{VERDICT[n.verdict]?.label ?? n.verdict}</span>
            </div>
            <p className="mt-1 text-[13px] text-mute">{n.numbers}</p>
            <div className="mt-1.5 flex gap-1">{n.refs.map((r) => <button key={r} onClick={() => onRef(r)} className="rounded bg-white/[0.07] px-1.5 py-px text-[10px] font-semibold text-mute hover:text-fin">{r}</button>)}</div>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import threading
import time

from fastapi import Body, FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from . import config
from .engine import analyst, research
from .engine.alerts import alerts, mark_seen
from .engine.digest import build_digest, set_triage, window
from .engine.enrich import people_card, summary_card
from .engine.results import results_card
from .llm import llm
from .portfolio import RESEARCH_PICKS, portfolio, rules, set_portfolio, set_rules
from .sources import nse
from .util import now_ist

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("finn")

app = FastAPI(title="FINN - Financial Investment Agent", version="1.0")
app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=800)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- meta & settings
@app.get("/api/meta")
def meta():
    return {"now": now_ist().isoformat(), "llm": llm.status(), "portfolio": portfolio(), "researchPicks": RESEARCH_PICKS,
            "rules": rules(), "offline": config.OFFLINE}


@app.get("/api/portfolio")
def get_portfolio():
    return portfolio()


@app.put("/api/portfolio")
def put_portfolio(items: list[dict] = Body(...)):
    return set_portfolio(items)


@app.get("/api/rules")
def get_rules():
    return rules()


@app.put("/api/rules")
def put_rules(body: dict = Body(...)):
    return set_rules(body)


@app.get("/api/search")
def search(q: str):
    q = q.strip().upper()
    if not q:
        return []
    try:
        master = nse.equity_master()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        master = []
    exact = [m for m in master if m["symbol"] == q]
    starts = [m for m in master if m["symbol"].startswith(q) and m["symbol"] != q]
    named = [m for m in master if q in m["name"].upper() and m not in starts and m not in exact]
    return (exact + starts + named)[:12]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- push
@app.get("/api/digest")
def digest(hours: float = 24, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None, fresh: bool = False):
    s, e = window(hours=hours, start=start, end=end)
    return build_digest(s, e, use_cache=not fresh)


@app.post("/api/enrich")
def enrich(body: dict = Body(...)):
    kind = body.get("kind")
    sym = body.get("symbol", "")
    if kind == "results":
        return results_card(sym, body.get("text", ""), body.get("ts"), body.get("url"))
    if kind == "people":
        extra = [u for u in body.get("urls") or [] if u and u != body.get("url")]
        return people_card(sym, body.get("company", sym), body.get("text", ""), body.get("url"), extra)
    if kind == "summary":
        return summary_card(sym, body.get("company", sym), body.get("desc", ""), body.get("text", ""), body.get("url"))
    raise HTTPException(400, "unknown enrichment kind")


@app.post("/api/triage")
def triage(body: dict = Body(...)):
    return set_triage(body["id"], body.get("state"))


@app.get("/api/alerts")
def get_alerts(days: int = 7):
    return alerts(days)


@app.post("/api/alerts/seen")
def alerts_seen():
    return {"seenAt": mark_seen()}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- pull
@app.get("/api/research/{symbol}")
def research_dossier(symbol: str):
    d = research.dossier(symbol)
    if not d:
        raise HTTPException(404, f"No fundamentals found for {symbol.upper()} - is it an NSE symbol?")
    return d


@app.get("/api/research/{symbol}/promises")
def research_promises(symbol: str):
    return analyst.promises(symbol)


@app.get("/api/research/{symbol}/thesis")
def research_thesis(symbol: str):
    return analyst.thesis(symbol)


@app.post("/api/research/{symbol}/ask")
def research_ask(symbol: str, body: dict = Body(...)):
    q = (body.get("q") or "").strip()
    if not q:
        raise HTTPException(400, "empty question")
    return analyst.ask(symbol, q)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- background refresh
def _refresher():
    """Keeps the 24h digest and alerts warm so the app opens instantly and new alerts are detected."""
    interval = int(os.getenv("FINN_REFRESH_SECONDS") or 900)
    while True:
        try:
            llm.warmup()
            s, e = window(hours=24)
            build_digest(s, e, use_cache=False)
            alerts(7)
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
            log.warning("background refresh failed: %s", ex)
        time.sleep(interval)


@app.on_event("startup")
def _start():
    if os.getenv("FINN_NO_BACKGROUND") != "1" and not config.OFFLINE:
        threading.Thread(target=_refresher, daemon=True, name="finn-refresher").start()
    elif llm.enabled:
        threading.Thread(target=llm.warmup, daemon=True, name="finn-llm-probe").start()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- frontend
if config.FRONTEND_DIST.exists():
    app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=config.FRONTEND_DIST / "assets"), name="assets")

    @app.get("/{path:path}")
    def spa(path: str):
        if path.startswith("api/"):
            raise HTTPException(404, "not found")
        root = config.FRONTEND_DIST.resolve()
        f = (root / path).resolve()
        if path and f.is_file() and root in f.parents:
            return FileResponse(f)
        return FileResponse(root / "index.html")

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Cpu, Plus, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { api } from "../api";
import type { Holding, Meta } from "../types";
import { SectionTitle } from "../components/ui";

const PURPOSE: Record<string, string> = {
  results_pdf_extract: "Results PDF → numbers (fallback)",
  mgmt_change_extract: "Management-change bio",
  filing_summary: "One-line filing summary",
  transcript_extract: "Transcript → guidance & claims",
  promise_vs_delivery: "Promise vs delivery judgement",
  thesis: "Narrative vs numbers, bull/bear",
  ask: "Ask the filings",
};

export default function Settings({ meta, reloadMeta }: { meta: Meta | null; reloadMeta: () => void }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<Holding[]>([]);
  const [q, setQ] = useState("");
  const [hits, setHits] = useState<{ symbol: string; name: string }[]>([]);
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => { if (meta) setItems(meta.portfolio); }, [meta]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!q.trim()) { setHits([]); return; }
    const t = setTimeout(() => api.search(q).then(setHits).catch(() => {}), 180);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [q]);

  const save = async (next: Holding[]) => {
    setItems(next);
    await api.portfolio(next);
    setSaved(true);
    setTimeout(() => setSaved(false), 1500);
    reloadMeta();
  };
  const total = items.reduce((a, h) => a + (Number(h.weight) || 0), 0);
  const u = meta?.llm.usage ?? {};

  return (
    <div className="pb-28">
      <SectionTitle right={<span className="text-[12px] text-mute">{items.length} stocks · {total.toFixed(0)}% {saved && <span className="text-up">· saved</span>}</span>}>Portfolio</SectionTitle>
      <div className="card divide-y divide-white/5">
        {items.map((h, i) => (
          <div key={h.symbol} className="flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-2.5">
            <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
              <div className="text-[13px] font-semibold">{h.symbol}</div>
              <div className="truncate text-[11px] text-mute">{h.sector}</div>
            </div>
            <input type="number" value={h.weight} min={0} max={100}
              onChange={(e) => setItems(items.map((x, j) => (j === i ? { ...x, weight: Number(e.target.value) } : x)))}
              onBlur={() => save(items)}
              className="w-16 rounded-lg bg-ink-800 px-2 py-1 text-right text-[13px] num" />
            <span className="text-[12px] text-mute">%</span>
            <button onClick={() => save(items.filter((_, j) => j !== i))} className="p-1 text-dim hover:text-down" aria-label={`Remove ${h.symbol}`}><Trash2 size={15} /></button>
          </div>
        ))}
        <div className="relative px-4 py-2.5">
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Plus size={15} className="text-fin" />
            <input value={q} onChange={(e) => setQ(e.target.value)} placeholder="Add any NSE stock…" className="flex-1 bg-transparent text-[13px] outline-none placeholder:text-dim" />
          </div>
          {hits.length > 0 && (
            <div className="mt-2 space-y-0.5">
              {hits.slice(0, 6).map((h) => (
                <button key={h.symbol} onClick={() => { save([...items, { symbol: h.symbol, weight: 3, sector: "" }]); setQ(""); }}
                  className="flex w-full items-baseline gap-2 rounded-lg px-2 py-1.5 text-left hover:bg-white/[0.04]">
                  <b className="text-[13px]">{h.symbol}</b><span className="truncate text-[12px] text-mute">{h.name}</span>
                </button>
              ))}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>

      <SectionTitle>AI routing & cost</SectionTitle>
      <div className="card p-4 text-[13px]">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <Cpu size={16} className={meta?.llm.enabled ? "text-fin" : "text-mute"} />
          <span className="font-semibold">{meta?.llm.enabled ? `On · ${meta.llm.provider}` : "Rules-only mode"}</span>
        </div>
        {meta?.llm.enabled && meta.llm.models && (
          <div className="mt-3 grid grid-cols-2 gap-2">
            <div className="rounded-xl bg-white/[0.03] p-3"><div className="text-[10.5px] uppercase tracking-wider text-mute">Fast tier · bulk reading</div><div className="mt-0.5 font-semibold">{meta.llm.models.fast}</div></div>
            <div className="rounded-xl bg-white/[0.03] p-3"><div className="text-[10.5px] uppercase tracking-wider text-mute">Smart tier · judgement</div><div className="mt-0.5 font-semibold">{meta.llm.models.smart}</div></div>
          </div>
        )}
        {!meta?.llm.enabled && <p className="mt-2 text-mute">Add a free Gemini key to <code className="text-white">backend/.env</code> to switch on transcript reading, bios and verdicts. Everything else already works without it.</p>}
        {meta?.llm.lastError && <p className="mt-2 text-[12px] text-warn">{meta.llm.lastError}</p>}
        <div className="mt-3 grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 text-center">
          <div><div className="text-[18px] font-semibold num">{u.calls ?? 0}</div><div className="text-[11px] text-mute">model calls</div></div>
          <div><div className="text-[18px] font-semibold num">{u.cached ?? 0}</div><div className="text-[11px] text-mute">served from cache</div></div>
          <div><div className="text-[18px] font-semibold num">{(((u.input_tokens ?? 0) + (u.output_tokens ?? 0)) / 1000).toFixed(1)}k</div><div className="text-[11px] text-mute">tokens</div></div>
        </div>
        {u.by_purpose && Object.keys(u.by_purpose).length > 0 && (
          <div className="mt-3 space-y-1 border-t hairline pt-3">
            {Object.entries(u.by_purpose).map(([k, v]) => (
              <div key={k} className="flex items-center gap-2 text-[12px]">
                <span className={v.tier === "smart" ? "text-info" : "text-fin"}>●</span>
                <span className="flex-1 text-white/85">{PURPOSE[k] ?? k}</span>
                <span className="text-mute num">{v.calls} calls · {v.cached} cached · {(v.tokens / 1000).toFixed(1)}k tok</span>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
        <p className="mt-3 text-[12px] leading-relaxed text-mute">
          Classification, scoring, results numbers (exchange XBRL), price signals and all ratios are computed with rules and code: free, instant, exact.
          The fast model only reads text that matters (filings with vague headlines, transcripts). The smart model only judges small, pre-computed fact packs.
        </p>
      </div>

      <SectionTitle>How FINN decides what matters</SectionTitle>
      <div className="card space-y-2 p-4 text-[13px] leading-relaxed text-white/85">
        <p><b>1. Collapse.</b> A results day produces 5-8 filings (outcome, press release, deck, newspaper ad, call invite). FINN folds them into one story.</p>
        <p><b>2. Score.</b> Category weight × your position size × how the stock actually reacted × your alert preferences.</p>
        <p><b>3. Explain.</b> Every card says why it's there. Price moves with no filing behind them get flagged - those are the ones to chase.</p>
        <p><b>4. Hide.</b> Routine paperwork (ESOP allotments, trading-window notices, compliance certificates) is counted, not shown.</p>
      </div>
      <p className="mt-6 text-center text-[11px] text-dim">FINN · data: NSE filings & XBRL, Yahoo EOD prices, screener.in documents · not investment advice</p>
    </div>
  );
}

Looking at this run before the routing change, with lite-model judging: the DIXON segment check worked correctly since the judge used a company row to verify segment volume when later calls lacked a segment number. For ASIANPAINT, the capex commitment of around 700 crores actually appears to have been exceeded, which contradicts an earlier run that flagged it as missed — likely just LLM variance between runs. The capex overshoot verdict itself is debatable though — the summary describes it as over-promising (committing 700 while actually spending 1,484), which doesn't square with calling it "delivered." Since capex direction is inherently ambiguous, I'm considering a clearer rule: spending within ±15% of the committed plan counts as delivered, while anything further off counts as missed, with a note on whether it was over or under. Applying this, DIXON's 1,058 against a 1,100–1,200 guidance range (-4% from the low end) would be delivered, while ASIANPAINT's 1,484 versus 700 (+112%) would be missed, specifically over-spent. This feels like a reasonable, transparent judgment call that I can document clearly in the README rather than leaving ambiguous. On LT's order inflow, I realize the earlier extraction conflated order book growth (28% YoY to Rs 7.40 trillion) with order inflow guidance — these aren't the same metric, so marking it "unverifiable" now is actually the more accurate call. I also want to update the "too early to tell" language to "limited track record" to match the newer phrasing convention. Once the thesis lines come through, I'll let the extraction stay cached since its prompt hasn't changed, but rerun the judge with the updated prompt and rules, plus let the summary refresh too — but first I need to finalize and add the capex rule before triggering that rerun. Fixed one gap — the segment guard now flags the DIXON mobile-volume claim as unverifiable. There's still a capex issue: ASIANPAINT's overshoot (₹700 Cr guided vs ₹1,484 Cr spent) is wrongly marked "delivered," so I'll add a documented rule where spending within ±15% of plan counts as delivered, otherwise it's missed with the direction noted.

● Bull vs. bear — a tight case each way. 
Worked example — numbers vs. narrative: take the last four quarters and, against management's 
own headline guidance and growth commentary, tell me what was promised vs. what was actually 
delivered. This is the difference between summarising management and analysing them — and it's 
the kind of thing we value most. 
One discipline for the pull side: ground it in the primary sources (annual reports + transcripts). No 
broker notes, no news, no research reports, and don't lean on the model's own outside knowledge 
of the company. Differentiated signal lives in primary data; secondary commentary is where it gets 
noisy. (Push-side enrichment like a person's professional background is a different thing and 
completely fine.) 
The interaction model — experiment 
How the investor interacts with all of this is entirely up to you, and we strongly encourage you to 
experiment. Chat, voice, a copilot, a dashboard, or something we haven't thought of — try more 
than the obvious. Everything mobile-first. The best submissions will show a point of view about how 
an investor should interact with this, not just what data to show. 
The bar — no AI slop 
Whatever you build: core, concise, beautifully presented, and interactive. It should save the investor 
time and show them what's important — and feel like a product someone thought hard about, not a 
model filling a template. Density and design both count. 
Tools, models & cost 
● No restriction on models. Use anything — open-source, local, or any commercial provider. 
Pick the right tool for each step; that choice is part of what we're evaluating. 
● This is comfortably doable on free tiers — you do not need to spend to compete. 
● Efficiency earns bonus points. The less you spend to achieve the same result, the better. 
Smart model routing (cheap models for bulk extraction, a stronger model only where 
reasoning demands it), caching, and chunking are exactly the instincts we're looking for. 
Scope, and how we grade 
● The deliverable is a mobile-first working prototype. We grade creativity, product sense, 
judgment, and architecture — not completeness. 

===== PAGE 4 =====
ENAM Holdings Pvt. Ltd.  
4
● Thin-but-working beats broad-but-broken. A focused prototype that nails one or two 
workflows beautifully beats a broad one that doesn't run. A demo that doesn't run is the 
worst outcome. 
● Build the smallest thing that proves you can build the real thing well. 
What to submit 
● The mobile-first prototype — a deployed link, Expo/TestFlight, or responsive web; however 
you ship it, make it easy for us to try on a phone. 
● The GitHub repository 
● Your AI build history — the coding-agent and LLM conversations you used while building 
(e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, or ChatGPT exports / share links). We want to see how you work 
with the tools, not just the finished code. 
● A short writeup (in your covering email) Cover what you built, the key decisions and trade-
offs, what you deliberately left out, and where you'd take it next. 
● Submit your response in an email with the links and attachments to assessment@enam.com 
with the subject line as “ENAM - IIT screening - 2027”

## Help Command Output
Global
  /help - show full help
  ? - show quick help
  / - commands
  @ - mention files
  # - mention issues and pull requests
  ! - execute shell command
  shift+tab - switch modes
  ctrl+s - stash/pop current prompt
  ctrl+q - enqueue prompt
  ctrl+r - reverse search history
  ctrl+o - toggle all timeline
  ctrl+c - cancel
  ctrl+c×2 - exit
  esc esc - clear input, interrupt, stop agents, or rewind
  ctrl+d - shutdown
  ctrl+z - suspend
  ctrl+l - clear screen
  ctrl+t - toggle reasoning display
  ctrl+x → b - move current task to background
  ctrl+x → g - collapse or expand the autopilot goal panel
  ctrl+x → o - open most recent link

Input
  ctrl+a - go to line start
  ctrl+e - go to line end
  ctrl+h - delete previous character
  ctrl+w - delete previous word
  ctrl+u - delete from cursor to beginning of line
  ctrl+k - delete from cursor to end of line
  meta+←/→ - move cursor by word
  shift+enter - insert newline
  ctrl+g - edit prompt in $EDITOR

Agent Environment
  /init - Initialize Gemini instructions for this repository
  /agent - Browse and select agents: /agent [name]
  /skills - Manage skills for enhanced capabilities
  /mcp - Manage MCP server configuration
  /plugin - Manage plugins and plugin marketplaces

Agents / Subagents
  /model - Select the AI model for this session (use 'auto' to let Gemini pick automatically). Use /config model to set the user default, '--repo'/'--local' to set the repo default, or 'plan'/'--plan' to set the plan-mode model.
  /delegate - Send this session to GitHub and Gemini will create a PR; use --base to choose the PR target branch
  /fleet - Enable fleet mode for parallel subagent execution
  /autopilot - Toggle autopilot mode, or set an autopilot objective with an optional AI-credit limit (--max-ai-credits)
  /tasks - View and manage tasks (subagents and shell commands)

Code
  /ide - Connect to an IDE workspace
  /diff - Review the changes made in the current directory
  /pr - Operate on pull requests for the current branch
  /review - Run code review agent to analyze changes
  /security-review - Analyze staged and unstaged changes for security vulnerabilities.
  /rubber-duck - Get an independent critique of your current work from the rubber duck agent
  /lsp - Manage language server configuration
  /terminal-setup - Configure terminal for multiline input support (shift+enter)

Permissions
  /permissions - Switch between permission modes
  /allow-all - Enable all permissions (tools, paths, and URLs)
  /sandbox - Manage sandbox settings, including file path permissions, network permissions, and more
  /add-dir - Allow file access to a directory and load its .github skills and agents as trusted configuration
  /list-dirs - Display allowed directories and exact session path grants
  /cwd - Change working directory or show current directory
  /reset-allowed-tools - Reset session tool and exact-path approvals

Session
  /resume - Switch sessions by local or cloud history ID, task ID, or name
  /rename - Rename the current session, or auto-generate a name from conversation
  /fork - Fork the current session into a new session, optionally with a name. Use `/fork worktree` to fork into a new worktree based on the current branch.
  /worktree - Create a new git worktree from your configured base ref and switch into it, leaving your uncommitted changes behind. Use `/new worktree` for an empty session or `/fork worktree` to preserve the current context. The deprecated `/worktree new` command still works for now.
  /move - Move your uncommitted changes into a new git worktree and switch into it. Pass a branch name, a task to start, or nothing to auto-name.
  /context - Show context window token usage and visualization
  /usage - Display session usage metrics and statistics
  /session - View and manage sessions. Use subcommands for details.
  /compact - Summarize conversation history to reduce context window usage. Optionally provide focus instructions.
  /share - Open sharing actions for this session, or export with file, html, gist, research, or link
  /remote - Share this session: remote control from GitHub web and mobile, or directly with another CLI
  /copy - Copy the last response to the clipboard
  /rewind - Rewind the last turn and revert file changes

Help
  /help - Show help for interactive commands
  /changelog - Display changelog for CLI versions. Add 'summarize' to get an AI summary.
  /feedback - Provide feedback about the CLI
  /diagnose - Analyze session logs, including why a permission request needed approval
  /theme - View or set color mode
  /statusline - Configure status line items
  /footer - Configure status line items

"""Tiny SQLite-backed cache + app state. One file, no server, safe across threads."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import threading
import time
from typing import Any

from .config import DB_PATH


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path=DB_PATH):
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self._db = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False, isolation_level=None)
        self._db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self._db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
        self._db.execute(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cache (ns TEXT, key TEXT, value TEXT, created REAL, PRIMARY KEY (ns, key))"
        )
        self._db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)")

    # ---- cache -------------------------------------------------------------
    def get(self, ns: str, key: str, max_age: float | None = None) -> Any | None:
        """Return cached JSON value, or None if missing / older than max_age seconds."""
        hit = self.get_with_age(ns, key)
        if hit is None:
            return None
        value, age = hit
        if max_age is not None and age > max_age:
            return None
        return value

    def get_with_age(self, ns: str, key: str) -> tuple[Any, float] | None:
        with self._lock:
            row = self._db.execute("SELECT value, created FROM cache WHERE ns=? AND key=?", (ns, key)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None
        return json.loads(row[0]), time.time() - row[1]

    def set(self, ns: str, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        payload = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
        with self._lock:
            self._db.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO cache (ns, key, value, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (ns, key, payload, time.time()),
            )

    def delete_ns(self, ns: str) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._db.execute("DELETE FROM cache WHERE ns=?", (ns,))

    # ---- state -------------------------------------------------------------
    def state(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
        with self._lock:
            row = self._db.execute("SELECT value FROM state WHERE key=?", (key,)).fetchone()
        return json.loads(row[0]) if row else default

    def set_state(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._db.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO state (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)", (key, json.dumps(value, default=str))
            )

    def update_state(self, key: str, fn, default: Any = None) -> Any:
        with self._lock:
            value = fn(self.state(key, default))
            self.set_state(key, value)
            return value


store = Store()

    body = ""

    changes, one_line, method = None, None, "rules"
    if llm.enabled and (body.strip() or headline):

                       purpose="mgmt_change_extract", max_tokens=2000, expect="changes")
        if isinstance(res, dict) and isinstance(res.get("changes"), list):
            src = (headline + "\n" + body).lower()
            # anti-hallucination: keep people whose surname actually appears in the filing
            changes = [c for c in res["changes"] if c.get("name") and c["name"].split()[-1].lower() in src]
            one_line = res.get("one_line")
            method = "llm"
    if not changes:

        method = "rules"
    for c in changes:

    card = {"kind": "people", "symbol": symbol, "changes": changes, "oneLine": one_line, "method": method,

    def get(self, url: str, headers: dict | None = None, retries: int = 3) -> httpx.Response:
        if OFFLINE:
            raise FetchError("offline mode")
        host = urlparse(url).netloc
        interval = HOST_INTERVAL.get(host, 0.0)
        last_exc: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(retries):
            with self._pace(host):
                wait = self._last_call.get(host, 0) + interval - time.time()
                if wait > 0:
                    time.sleep(wait)
                self._last_call[host] = time.time()
            try:
                r = self.client.get(url, headers=headers)
                if r.status_code == 200:
                    return r
                if r.status_code in (404, 410):
                    raise FetchError(f"{r.status_code} for {url}")
                last_exc = FetchError(f"HTTP {r.status_code} for {url}")
            except httpx.HTTPError as e:
                last_exc = e
            except FetchError:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.8 * (2**attempt))
        raise FetchError(str(last_exc))

    # ---- cached helpers ------------------------------------------------------
    def _cached(self, ns: str, url: str, ttl: float, fetch) -> Any:
        hit = store.get_with_age(ns, url)
        if hit is not None and hit[1] <= ttl:
            return hit[0]
        try:
            value = fetch()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure falls back to stale cache
            if hit is not None:
                log.warning("using stale cache for %s (%s)", url, e)
                return hit[0]
            raise FetchError(str(e)) from e
        store.set(ns, url, value)
        return value

    def json(self, url: str, ns: str, ttl: float, headers: dict | None = None) -> Any:
        return self._cached(ns, url, ttl, lambda: self.get(url, headers=headers).json())

    def text(self, url: str, ns: str, ttl: float, headers: dict | None = None) -> str:
        return self._cached(ns, url, ttl, lambda: self.get(url, headers=headers).text)

    def file(self, url: str, headers: dict | None = None) -> Path:
        """Download once, keep forever (filings never change)."""
        digest = hashlib.sha1(url.encode()).hexdigest()

"""NSE: corporate announcements, integrated-filing financials (structured), equity master."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import logging
import re
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from urllib.parse import quote

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

from ..http import http
from ..util import crore, num, parse_day, parse_nse_dt

log = logging.getLogger("finn.nse")

API = "https://www.nseindia.com/api"
HDRS = {
    "Accept": "application/json, text/plain, */*",
    "Referer": "https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-announcements",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- announcements
def announcements(symbol: str, start: date, end: date) -> list[dict]:
    url = (f"{API}/corporate-announcements?index=equities&symbol={quote(symbol)}"
           f"&from_date={start:%d-%m-%Y}&to_date={end:%d-%m-%Y}")
    ttl = 600 if end >= date.today() else 7 * 86400
    raw = http.json(url, ns="nse_ann", ttl=ttl, headers=HDRS) or []
    out = []
    for x in raw:
        ts = parse_nse_dt(x.get("an_dt") or x.get("sort_date"))
        out.append({
            "id": str(x.get("seq_id") or f"{x.get('symbol')}-{x.get('dt')}"),
            "symbol": x.get("symbol") or symbol,
            "company": x.get("sm_name") or symbol,
            "industry": x.get("smIndustry"),
            "ts": ts.isoformat() if ts else None,
            "desc": (x.get("desc") or "").strip(),
            "text": (x.get("attchmntText") or "").strip(),
            "url": x.get("attchmntFile") or None,
            "size": x.get("attFileSize"),
        })
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- equity master
def equity_master() -> list[dict]:
    text = http.text("https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/equities/EQUITY_L.csv", ns="nse_master", ttl=7 * 86400)
    rows = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        r = {k.strip(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k}
        if r.get("SERIES") in ("EQ", "BE", "BZ", "SM", "ST"):
            out.append({"symbol": r["SYMBOL"], "name": r["NAME OF COMPANY"], "isin": r.get("ISIN NUMBER")})
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- integrated filings
def integrated_filings(symbol: str) -> list[dict]:
    """All structured 'Integrated Filing - Financials' for a symbol (newest first)."""
    url = (f"{API}/integrated-filing-results?index=equities&symbol={quote(symbol)}"
           f"&type=Integrated%20Filing-%20Financials")
    data = http.json(url, ns="nse_ifr", ttl=1800, headers=HDRS) or {}
    out = []
    for x in data.get("data", []) if isinstance(data, dict) else []:
        qe = parse_day(x.get("qe_Date"))
        if not qe or not x.get("ixbrl"):
            continue

def _safe(fn, *a):
    try:
        return fn(*a)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("%s%s failed: %s", fn.__name__, a[:1], e)
        return None

_TABLE = re.compile(r"revenue from operations|total income from operations|interest earned", re.I)
_INTIMATION = re.compile(r"(is|are) scheduled|will be held|to be held|to consider and approve|intimation of (the )?board meeting", re.I)
_SUBJECT = re.compile(r"\b(?:sub(?:ject)?|re)\s*[:\-–]\s*(.{12,260}?)(?:\n\s*\n|\bdear\b|\bsir\b|\bmadam\b|\bref(?:erence)?\b|$)", re.I | re.S)

DIGEST_VERSION = "d4"


def build_digest(start: datetime, end: datetime, use_cache: bool = True) -> dict:
    cache_key = f"{DIGEST_VERSION}|{start.isoformat()[:16]}|{end.isoformat()[:15]}"
    if use_cache:
        hit = store.get("digest", cache_key, max_age=300)
        if hit:
            return _apply_triage(hit)

    holdings = portfolio()
    weights = {h["symbol"]: h.get("weight", 0) for h in holdings}
    sectors = {h["symbol"]: h.get("sector", "") for h in holdings}
    symbols = list(weights)
    r = rules()
    fetch_from = min(start.date(), (now_ist() - timedelta(days=21)).date())

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex:
        anns = dict(zip(symbols, ex.map(lambda s: _safe(nse.announcements, s, fetch_from, end.date()) or [], symbols)))
        sigs = dict(zip(symbols, ex.map(lambda s: _safe(signals, s, int(r.get("volumeLookback", 20))), symbols)))

    names = {s: (sigs[s] or {}).get("name") for s in symbols}
    all_items, upcoming = [], []
    for sym, lst in anns.items():
        for a in lst:
            if not a.get("ts"):
                continue
            c = classify(a["desc"], a["text"])
            it = {**a, **c, "headline": clean_headline(a["text"], a["desc"])}
            names[sym] = names.get(sym) or a["company"]
            all_items.append(it)

    # ---- upcoming events from the last 3 weeks of filings --------------------------------
    today = now_ist().date()
    for it in all_items:
        if it["subtype"] in ("intimation", "notice", "record_date", "board_intimation") or it["category"] in ("agm_egm", "dividend"):
            future = sorted({d for d in find_dates(it["text"]) if today <= d <= today + timedelta(days=45)})
            if future:
                label = {"intimation": "Results (board meeting)", "notice": "Earnings call", "record_date": "Record date",
                         "board_intimation": "Board meeting"}.get(it["subtype"], CATEGORIES[it["category"]])
                upcoming.append({"date": future[0].isoformat(), "symbol": it["symbol"], "label": label,
                                 "detail": it["headline"] or it["why"], "url": it["url"]})
    seen_up = set()
    upcoming = [u for u in sorted(upcoming, key=lambda u: u["date"])
                if not ((u["symbol"], u["label"]) in seen_up or seen_up.add((u["symbol"], u["label"])))][:12]

    items = [it for it in all_items if start <= datetime.fromisoformat(it["ts"]) <= end]

    # ---- refine ambiguous, potentially material filings by peeking at the PDF ------------
    ambiguous = [it for it in items if it.get("url") and (
        it["subtype"] in ("board_outcome", "unknown_role", "other") or
        (it["category"] == "credit_rating" and it["subtype"] == "unknown") or
        (it["subtype"] == "news" and not it["headline"]))][:30]
    if ambiguous:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex:
            list(ex.map(_refine, ambiguous))

    # ---- collapse into events ------------------------------------------------------------
    results_syms = {it["symbol"] for it in items if it["category"] == "results" and it["subtype"] == "filed"}
    groups: dict[tuple, list] = defaultdict(list)
    for it in items:
        cat = it["category"]
        if cat == "earnings_call" and it["symbol"] in results_syms:
            cat = "results"
        fam = cat if cat in ("results", "management_change", "earnings_call", "unclassified", "investor_meetings") else f"{cat}:{it['subtype']}"
        groups[(it["symbol"], fam)].append(it)

    events, muted = [], 0
    for (sym, fam), its in groups.items():
        its.sort(key=lambda x: (x["score"], x["ts"]), reverse=True)
        p = its[0]
        cat = fam.split(":")[0]
        pref = r["categories"].get(cat, "digest")
        if pref == "mute":
            muted += len(its)
            continue
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(p["ts"])
        w = weights.get(sym, 0)
        score = p["score"] + min(8.0, w * 0.8)
        why = [CATEGORIES.get(cat, cat)]
        if w:
            why.append(f"{w:g}% of portfolio")

def _apply_triage(d: dict) -> dict:
    tri = store.state("triage", {})
    for e in d["top"] + d["watch"]:
        e["triage"] = (tri.get(e["id"]) or {}).get("state")
    return d


def set_triage(event_id: str, state: str | None) -> dict:
    def upd(t):
        t = t or {}
        if state:
            t[event_id] = {"state": state, "t": now_ist().isoformat()}
        else:
            t.pop(event_id, None)
        return t
    return store.update_state("triage", upd, {})


def window(hours: float | None = None, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    if start:
        s = datetime.fromisoformat(start)
        s = s if s.tzinfo else s.replace(tzinfo=IST)
        e = datetime.fromisoformat(end) if end else now_ist()
        e = e if e.tzinfo else e.replace(tzinfo=IST)
        return s, e
    e = now_ist()
    return e - timedelta(hours=hours or 24), e

Contents of https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing:
This guide provides an overview of different Gemini API billing options, explains how to enable billing and monitor usage, and provides answers to frequently asked questions (FAQs) about billing.

## About billing and tiers

Billing for the Gemini API is based on your payment history.

| Usage tier | Qualification                                                                  | [Billing tier cap](#spend-caps) |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| **Free**   | [Active project](/gemini-api/docs/api-key#google-cloud-projects) or free trial | N/A                             |
| **Tier 1** | [Set up and link an active billing account](#setup-billing)                    | $250                            |
| **Tier 2** | Paid $100 + 3 days from first successful payment                               | $2,000                          |
| **Tier 3** | Paid $1,000 + 30 days from first successful payment                            | $20,000 - $100,000+             |

New accounts begin on the Free Tier, which allows access to [certain models](/gemini-api/docs/pricing) in the Gemini API and AI Studio, up to the models' free tier [rate limits](https://aistudio.google.com/rate-limit).

To deploy your applications directly from Build mode, eligible accounts can use the **Google Cloud Starter Tier**. This tier lets you publish up to 2 full-stack applications without setting up a Google Cloud project or billing account. See [Deploying from Google AI Studio](/gemini-api/docs/aistudio-deploying#starter-tier-eligibility) for eligibility details and refer to the [Google Cloud Starter Tier documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/starter-tier) for more information.

To access higher rate limits, use advanced models, and ensure your prompts and responses are **not** used to improve Google products\*, you can [link a billing account](#setup-billing) and [Prepay](#prepay) to move to the Paid Tiers. Then, you'll move through higher tiers based on cumulative spend and account age.

Tiers, rate limits, and billing account caps are all determined at the [billing account](#cloud-billing) level.

\* _Enterprise-grade data privacy: For more information on data use for paid services, see the [Terms of Service](/gemini-api/terms#data-use-paid)._

## Set up billing to access the Paid Tier

You can create a project and set up billing, or import an existing project, to upgrade to the Paid Tier in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/projects). Upgrading from the Free Tier to the Paid Tier means linking a billing account and [prepaying](#prepay) to add a minimum of $5 (or equivalent in other currencies) of credits to your account.

1.  Go to the AI Studio [API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys) page, [Projects](https://aistudio.google.com/projects) page, or anywhere you see **Set up billing** button in AI Studio.
    *   New users will have a [project and API key](/gemini-api/docs/api-key#google-cloud-projects) created for them by default.
    *   If you need a new key, click [**Create API key**](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys) and follow the dialog to add a key-project pair to the table.
2.  Find the Free Tier project you want to upgrade to the Paid Tier, and click **Set up billing** under the _Billing Tier_ column.
3.  If you've never set up a Google billing account before:
    *   You'll be asked to select your country to agree to the Terms of Service.
    *   Then, fill in or confirm your contact information and payment method to continue.
4.  If you have set up Google billing accounts in the past:
    *   You'll be asked to choose from your existing billing accounts.
    *   If you don't want to use any of your existing accounts, click **Add new billing account** and fill in or confirm your contact information and payment method to continue.
5.  Next, you will either be:
    *   Asked to prepay a minimum of $5 to complete billing setup (meaning your account is auto-assigned to the [Prepay](#prepay) billing plan),
    *   Given the choice between [Prepay](#prepay) and [Postpay](#postpay) billing plans for your account.
    *   Assigned to a [Postpay](#postpay) billing plan for an intermediary period until the new Prepay system propagates to all users (starting March 23, 2026).
6.  After prepaying or selecting Postpay, your account setup is complete.

### Upgrade to the next paid tier

If you're already on a paid tier and meet the [criteria](#about-billing) for a plan change, you will be automatically upgraded to the next tier (subject to [processing times](#processing-times)).

## Verify billing status

After you have [linked a billing account](#setup-billing) to your project, you can monitor its status on the [AI Studio Billing page](https://aistudio.google.com/billing). Unlike the free tier, paid tier status is dynamic; while your usage tier is determined by your account history, the Gemini API will only serve requests if you have a positive [Prepay](#prepay) credit balance.

On the [Projects](https://aistudio.google.com/projects) page, you'll be able to see your project's tier and billing plan under the _Billing Tier_ column. Any billing status actions you may need to take for a project display in the _Billing Tier_ or _Status_ columns:

*   "**_Set up billing_**" if the project doesn't have a billing account attached.
*   "**_Set up Prepay_**" if the project does have a billing account attached, but is required to use a [Prepay](#prepay) billing plan that needs to be set up.
*   "**_No credits_**" if the billing account is required to purchase credits but the Prepay payments account isn't set up or the available credit balance is depleted.

Click any of the messages to proceed with the necessary actions.

## Monitor usage

You can monitor your usage of the Gemini API in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/usage) in **Dashboard** > **Usage**.

## Billing plans

Billing plans for the Gemini API and AI Studio fall into two categories that determine when you pay for usage: Prepay and Postpay. You can check your assigned billing plan and manage payment methods on the [AI Studio Billing](https://aistudio.google.com/billing) page.

### Prepay

In the Prepay billing plan, you purchase credits towards your prepay balance in advance of your Gemini API usage, and your API usage costs are deducted from your Prepay credit balance in [near real-time](#processing-times). You can prepay by [adding credits](#buy-credits) into your account, or setting up [auto-reload](#auto-reload). After credits are purchased, unused credits expire after 12 months and are [non-refundable](#refunds), except after [switching to a Postpay account](#postpay).

When your Prepay credit balance on the billing account hits $0, all API keys in all projects linked to that billing account will stop working simultaneously. Requests then fail with an [HTTP 402 Payment Required](/gemini-api/docs/api-error

#### Required roles

To deploy from source with build, you or your administrator must grant the Cloud Build service account the following IAM roles.

#### Click to view required roles for the Cloud Build service account

Cloud Build automatically uses the [Compute Engine default service account](/build/docs/cloud-build-service-account) as the default Cloud Build service account to build your source code and Cloud Run resource, unless you override this behavior. For Cloud Build to build your sources, ask your administrator to grant [Cloud Run Builder](/iam/docs/roles-permissions/run#run.builder) (`roles/run.builder`) to the Compute Engine default service account on your project:

  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \
      --member=serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com \
      --role=roles/run.builder
  

Replace `PROJECT_NUMBER` with your Google Cloud project number, and `PROJECT_ID` with your Google Cloud project ID. For detailed instructions on how to find your project ID, and project number, see [Creating and managing projects](/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects#identifying_projects).

Granting the Cloud Run builder role to the Compute Engine default service account takes a couple of minutes to [propagate](/iam/docs/access-change-propagation).

 

For a list of IAM roles and permissions that are associated with Cloud Run, see [Cloud Run IAM roles](/run/docs/reference/iam/roles) and [Cloud Run IAM permissions](/run/docs/reference/iam/permissions). If your Cloud Run service interfaces with Google Cloud APIs, such as Cloud Client Libraries, see the [service identity configuration guide](/run/docs/configuring/services/service-identity). For more information about granting roles, see [deployment permissions](/run/docs/reference/iam/roles#additional-configuration) and [manage access](/iam/docs/granting-changing-revoking-access).

### Deploy with build

To deploy from source code, click the tab for instructions on using the tool of your choice.

### gcloud

1.  In the Google Cloud console, activate Cloud Shell.

    [Activate Cloud Shell](https://console.cloud.google.com/?cloudshell=true)

    At the bottom of the Google Cloud console, a [Cloud Shell](/shell/docs/how-cloud-shell-works) session starts and displays a command-line prompt. Cloud Shell is a shell environment with the Google Cloud CLI already installed and with values already set for your current project. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.

2.  Change to your source directory. The source directory uses a Dockerfile if present, although it's not required.

3.  Build and deploy your service:

    gcloud run deploy SERVICE --source .

    Replace `SERVICE` with the name you want for your service.

4.  Respond to any prompts to install required APIs by responding `y` when prompted. You only need to do this once for a project. Respond to other prompts by supplying the platform and region, if you haven't set defaults for these as described in the [setup](/run/docs/setup) page.

5.  Wait for the build and deploy to complete. When finished, Cloud Run displays a success message.

After deployment, this service revision serves 100% of traffic.

### Compose

You can store your [Compose specification](https://compose-spec.io) in a `YAML` file and then deploy it from source code as a Cloud Run service using a single gcloud command.

1.  Change to your source directory. The source directory uses a Dockerfile if present, although it's not required.

2.  In your project directory, create a `compose.yaml` file with your service definitions.

    services:
      web:
        build: .
        ports:
          - "8080:8080"

    You can also specify more configuration options such as environment variables, secrets, and volume mounts.

**Deploy the services**

1.  To deploy the services, run the `gcloud run compose up` command:

    gcloud run compose up compose.yaml

2.  Respond `y` to any prompts to install required components or to enable APIs.

3.  Optional: [Make your service public](/run/docs/authenticating/public) if you want to allow unauthenticated access to the service.

After deployment, the Cloud Run service URL is displayed. Copy this URL and paste it into your browser to view the running container. You can disable the default authentication from the Google Cloud console.

## Deploy prebuilt source

You can deploy prebuilt source artifacts directly to Cloud Run, bypassing the Cloud Build step. The way this works is that instead of building a container image from source, you can upload a pre-packaged archive of your application directly to a Cloud Storage bucket. Cloud Run then takes this archive and runs it directly on a base image. This approach lets you develop and iterate fast locally and results in dramatically faster deployment times.

### Limitations

Deploying prebuilt source only supports the following:

*   Cloud Run services.
*   [Supported runtimes](/run/docs/runtime-support) (no Dockerfile support).
*   Source archive (.tar.gz) <= 250 MiB.
*   Binary (for example, go binary) or script (for example, python script) must be compatible with x86 architecture.
*   The source has to be self-contained, with all the dependencies packaged. The runtime base image only contains the minimum operating system and a few language libraries.

### Before you deploy prebuilt source

To use the "deploy without build" feature:

*   Make sure you have followed the steps in [Before you begin](#before_you_begin).
*   Enable the Cloud Run and Cloud Storage APIs:

    gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com \
      storage.googleapis.com

*   You must install the application dependencies locally before deploying, as they won't be installed (no build).

### Deploy without build

This section describes how to deploy your prebuilt source directly to Cloud Run.

### gcloud

To deploy prebuilt source from a local directory, use the `--no-build` flag to tell the `deploy` command to bypass the Cloud Build step:

gcloud beta run deploy SERVICE_NAME \
  --source APPLICATION_PATH \
  --no-build \
  --base-image=BASE_IMAGE \
  --command=COMMAND \
  --args=ARG

Replace the following:

*   `SERVICE_NAME`: the name of your Cloud Run service.
*   `APPLICATION_PATH`: the location of your application on the local file system.
*   `BASE_IMAGE`: the [runtime base image](/run/docs/configuring/services/runtime-base-images#how_to_obtain_base_images) you want to use for your application. For example, `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/serverless-runtimes/google-24/runtimes/nodejs24`. You could also use the short alias `nodejs24`.

    You can also deploy a pre-compiled binary without configuring additional language-specific runtime components using the OS only base image, such as `osonly24`. For more information, see [OS only runtime](/docs/buildpacks/osonly) in the buildpacks documentation.

*   `COMMAND`: the command that the container starts up with. Optional. If you don't specify a command, the base image will infer the container starting command at runtime.

*   `ARG`: an argument you send to the container command. If you use multiple arguments, specify each on its own line. Optional. If you don't specify arguments, the base image will infer any arguments at runtime.

### YAML

You can store your service specification in a YAML file and then deploy it using the gcloud CLI or the Google Cloud console `service.yaml` editor.

1.  Create a storage bucket to hold your application:

    gcloud storage buckets create gs://BUCKET_NAME --location=BUCKET_LOCATION

    Replace the following:

    *   `BUCKET_NAME`: the name you want to give your bucket, subject to [naming requirements](/storage/docs/buckets#naming). For example, `my-bucket`.
    *   `BUCKET_LOCATION`: the [location](/storage/docs/locations) of your bucket. For example, `US`.
2.  Create an archive with your application source using either zip or tar, for example:

    tar -cvzf ARCHIVE_NAME APPLICATION_PATH

    Replace the following:

    *   `ARCHIVE_NAME`: the name of the archive to create. For example, `app.tar.gz`.
    *   `APPLICATION_PATH`: the location of your application on the local file system. For example, `~/my-application`. To archive the current working directory, set this value to `*`.
3.  Upload your application archive to Cloud Storage:

    gcloud storage cp ARCHIVE_NAME gs://BUCKET_NAME

    Replace the following:

    *   `ARCHIVE_NAME`: the local path to the archive you created previously. For example, `app.tar.gz`.
    *   `BUCKET_NAME`: the name of the bucket you created previously. For example, `my-bucket`.
4.  Create a new `service.yaml` file with the following content:

    apiVersion: serving.knative.dev/v2
    kind: Service
    metadata:
     name: SERVICE_NAME
    spec:
     template:
       metadata:
         annotations:
           run.googleapis.com/sources: '{"": "gs://BUCKET_NAME/ARCHIVE_NAME"}'
           run.googleapis.com/base-images: '{"": "BASE_IMAGE"}'
       spec:
         containers:
         - image: scratch
           command:
           - COMMAND
           args:
           - ARG1
           - ARG-N
         runtimeClassName: run.googleapis.com/linux-base-image-update

    Replace the following:

    *   `SERVICE_NAME`: the name of your Cloud Run service. Service names must be 49 characters or less and must be unique per region and project.
    *   `BUCKET_NAME`: the name of the bucket you created previously. For example, `my-bucket`.
    *   `ARCHIVE_NAME`: the local path to the archive you created previously. For example, [`app.tar.gz`](http://app.tar.gz).
    *   `BASE_IMAGE`: the runtime base image you want to use for your application. For example, `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/serverless-runtimes/google-24/runtimes/nodejs24`.

        You can also deploy a pre-compiled binary without configuring additional language-specific runtime components using the OS only base image, such as `osonly24`. For more information

| .NET                                     | [Deploy a .NET service](/run/docs/quickstarts/build-and-deploy/deploy-dotnet-service)    | [Configure .NET buildpacks](/docs/buildpacks/build-application) |

Read more details about [supported language versions](/run/docs/runtime-support).

## Deploy from source with build

This section describes how to use [Google Cloud's buildpacks](/docs/buildpacks/overview) and Cloud Build to automatically build container images from your source code without having to install Docker on your machine or set up buildpacks or Cloud Build.

### Limitations

*   Deploy from source uses Artifact Registry and Cloud Build, so this feature is only available in [regions supported by Artifact Registry](/artifact-registry/docs/repo-locations#location-r) and [Cloud Build](/build/docs/locations).
*   Deploying from source is a convenience feature, and does not allow full customization of the build. For more control, build the container image using Cloud Build, for example, using `gcloud builds submit`, and then [deploy the container image](/run/docs/deploying) using, for example, `gcloud run deploy --image`.
*   Deploying from source with Google Cloud's buildpacks sets the Last Modified Date of source files to Jan 1, 1980. This is the default behavior of buildpacks and is designed to support [reproducible builds](https://reproducible-builds.org/). Depending on your language framework, this can affect browser-side caching of static files. If your application is affected by this, Google recommends disabling `etag` and `Last-Modified` HTTP headers in your application.
*   Deploying from source with Google Cloud's buildpacks always uses `gcr.io/buildpacks/builder:latest`. If your preferred language or OS configuration is not available in `latest`, [use a specific builder](/docs/buildpacks/use-a-specific-builder) to create an application image using your preferred builder.
*   You can deploy your service from source using Kotlin and other JVM languages such as [Java](/docs/buildpacks/java). The language you use must conform to the following rules:

    *   You can build the application using Maven or Gradle.
    *   The build file contains all the plugins required to produce classes.

### Before you deploy with build

Before you deploy from source with build:

*   Follow the steps in [Before you begin](#before_you_begin).

*   Enable the Cloud Build API, if it is not already enabled.

    **Roles required to enable APIs**

    To enable APIs, you need the `serviceusage.services.enable` permission. If you created the project, then you likely already have this permission through the Owner role (`roles/owner`). Otherwise, you can get this permission through the Service Usage Admin role (`roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin`). [Learn how to grant roles](/iam/docs/granting-changing-revoking-access).

    [Enable the API](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/enableflow?apiid=cloudbuild.googleapis.com)

"""PDF / ZIP attachment -> per-page text, cached. Filings are immutable so we extract once."""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import logging
import re
import zipfile

import pymupdf

from ..http import http
from ..store import store

log = logging.getLogger("finn.pdf")


def _pdf_bytes_pages(data: bytes, max_pages: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
    doc = pymupdf.open(stream=data, filetype="pdf")
    pages = []
    for i, page in enumerate(doc):
        if max_pages and i >= max_pages:
            break
        pages.append(page.get_text("text"))
    return pages


def document_pages(url: str, max_pages: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Text of each page of a filing (PDF, or PDFs inside a ZIP). Empty list if unreadable."""
    key = f"{url}|{max_pages or 0}"
    cached = store.get("pdftext", key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    try:
        path = http.file(url)
        data = path.read_bytes()
        if data[:4] == b"%PDF":
            pages = _pdf_bytes_pages(data, max_pages)
        elif data[:2] == b"PK":
            pages = []
            with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:
                for name in sorted(zf.namelist()):
                    if name.lower().endswith(".pdf"):
                        pages += _pdf_bytes_pages(zf.read(name), max_pages)
        else:
            pages = []
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("could not read %s: %s", url, e)
        return []
    store.set("pdftext", key, pages)
    return pages


def has_text(pages: list[str]) -> bool:
    return sum(len(p.strip()) for p in pages) > 200


def find_pages(pages: list[str], patterns: list[str], top: int = 5) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the pages that best match the given regex patterns (case-insensitive)."""
    scored = []
    for i, text in enumerate(pages):
        score = sum(len(re.findall(p, text, re.I)) for p in patterns)
        if score:
            scored.append((score, i))
    scored.sort(reverse=True)
    return sorted(i for _, i in scored[:top])

"""Alerts = events that cross the user's own thresholds (filing types they care about,
price / volume moves beyond their limits). Same engine as the digest, different lens."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

from ..portfolio import rules
from ..store import store
from ..util import now_ist
from .digest import build_digest, window


def alerts(days: int = 7) -> dict:
    s, e = window(hours=days * 24)
    d = build_digest(s, e)
    r = rules()
    out = []
    for ev in d["top"] + d["watch"]:
        if ev["category"] == "move":
            out.append({**ev, "trigger": "threshold"})
        elif r["categories"].get(ev["category"]) == "alert" and ev.get("base", ev["score"]) >= 55:
            out.append({**ev, "trigger": "category"})
    out.sort(key=lambda x: x["ts"], reverse=True)
    seen = store.state("alerts_seen_at")
    seen_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(seen) if seen else None
    for a in out:
        a["new"] = seen_dt is None or datetime.fromisoformat(a["ts"]) > seen_dt
    return {"alerts": out, "unseen": sum(1 for a in out if a["new"]), "rules": r, "generatedAt": d["generatedAt"]}


def mark_seen() -> str:
    t = now_ist().isoformat()
    store.set_state("alerts_seen_at", t)
    return t

"""LLM router.

* One OpenAI-compatible client (Gemini by default; Groq/OpenRouter work by changing .env).
* Two tiers, routed by *thinking budget* as well as model:
    fast  -> flash-class model with reasoning off: bulk extraction, ~1-5 s, no thinking tokens
    smart -> flash-class model with low reasoning: judgement over small, pre-computed fact packs
* Tiers are *chains*, not single models. Models are discovered from the provider, probed for
  latency in the background, and any 503 / 429 / timeout falls straight through to the next
  model (the failing one sits out for a few minutes). Model churn never breaks the app.

def _cached_card(ns: str, ident: str) -> dict | None:
    """With a key: the AI card. Without one: replay an AI card computed earlier if we have it, else the rules card."""
    if not llm.enabled:
        hit = store.get(ns, "llm|" + ident)
        if hit is not None:
            return {**hit, "replay": True}
    return store.get(ns, ("llm|" if llm.enabled else "rules|") + ident)


def people_card(symbol: str, company: str, headline: str, url: str | None, extra_urls: list[str] | None = None) -> dict:
    key = ("llm|" if llm.enabled else "rules|") + (url or f"{symbol}|{headline}")
    cached = _cached_card("people", url or f"{symbol}|{headline}")
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    body = ""
    for u in [url, *(extra_urls or [])][:3]:
        if u:
            body += "\n".join(document_pages(u, max_pages=15)) + "\n\n"
    changes, one_line, method = None, None, "rules"
    if llm.enabled and (body.strip() or headline):
        res = llm.json("fast", SYSTEM_PEOPLE, PROMPT_PEOPLE.format(company=company, headline=headline, body=body[:16000]),
                       purpose="mgmt_change_extract", max_tokens=2000, expect="changes")
        if isinstance(res, dict) and isinstance(res.get("changes"), list):
            src = (headline + "\n" + body).lower()
            # anti-hallucination: keep people whose surname actually appears in the filing
            changes = [c for c in res["changes"] if c.get("name") and c["name"].split()[-1].lower() in src]
            one_line = res.get("one_line")
            method = "llm"
    if not changes:
        changes = _regex_people(headline, body)
        method = "rules"
    for c in changes:
        c["linkedin"] = linkedin_search(c["name"], company)
    card = {"kind": "people", "symbol": symbol, "changes": changes, "oneLine": one_line, "method": method,
            "source": {"url": url}}
    store.set("people", key, card)
    return card

def _replay(ns: str, sym: str) -> dict | None:
    """No LLM key: serve the last AI analysis computed for this stock (labelled with its date) if one exists."""
    hit = store.get_with_age(ns, f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|llm")
    if not hit:
        return None
    value, age = hit
    return {**value, "replay": True, "replayedFrom": datetime.fromtimestamp(datetime.now().timestamp() - age).date().isoformat()}


def promises(symbol: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    key = f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}"
    cached = store.get("promises", key, max_age=12 * 3600)
    if cached:
        return cached
    if not llm.enabled and (replay := _replay("promises", sym)):
        return replay
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"symbol": sym, "error": "No fundamentals found for this ticker"}
    ts = transcripts(sym, 6)  # ~18 months of calls, so annual guidance has time to come due
    if not ts:
        return {"symbol": sym, "calls": [], "items": [], "claims": [], "message": "No readable concall transcripts found."}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(3) as ex:
        extracted = list(ex.map(lambda t: _extract_one(d["name"], t), ts))
    items = [g for e in extracted for g in e["guidance"]]
    claims = [c for e in extracted for c in e["claims"]]
    reported = [r for e in extracted for r in e.get("reported", [])]
    actuals_text, _ = _actuals(d)
    latest = d["trajectory"]["quarters"][-1]["p"] if d["trajectory"]["quarters"] else "n/a"
    ev_end = _evidence_end(d, extracted)
    for g in items:
        end = horizon_end(g.get("horizon"), _iso(g.get("callDate")))
        g["horizonEnd"] = end.isoformat() if end else None
        g["status"] = "closed" if end and ev_end and end <= ev_end else "open"
