def thesis(symbol: str) -> dict:
    sym = symbol.upper()
    key = f"{sym}|{PROMPT_VERSION}|{'llm' if llm.enabled else 'none'}"
    cached = store.get("thesis", key, max_age=12 * 3600)
    if cached:
        return cached
    if not llm.enabled and (replay := _replay("thesis", sym)):
        return replay
    d = dossier(sym)
    if not d:
        return {"symbol": sym, "error": "No fundamentals found for this ticker"}
    facts = _facts(d)
    p = promises(sym) if d else {}
    claims = [(f"C{i + 1}", c) for i, c in enumerate((p.get("claims") or [])[:10])]
    track = (f"{p['score']['credibility']}% of judged guidance delivered ({p['score']['judged']} judged); pattern: {p.get('pattern')}"
             if p.get("score", {}).get("credibility") is not None else "not enough judged guidance")
    out = {"symbol": sym, "facts": [{"id": i, "text": t} for i, t in facts],
           "claims": [{"id": i, "text": c.get("claim"), "quote": c.get("quote"), "page": c.get("page"), "call": c.get("callQuarter"),
                       "url": c.get("url")} for i, c in claims],
           "narrative": [], "bull": [], "bear": [], "watch": [], "oneLiner": None, "method": "rules"}
    valid = {i for i, _ in facts} | {i for i, _ in claims}
    if llm.enabled:
        res = llm.json("smart", SYSTEM_THESIS, PROMPT_THESIS.format(
            name=d["name"], facts="\n".join(f"{i}: {t}" for i, t in facts),
            claims="\n".join(f"{i} ({c.get('callQuarter')} call, p.{c.get('page')}): \"{c.get('quote')}\"" for i, c in claims) or "none",
            track=track), purpose="thesis", max_tokens=3000, temperature=0.2, expect="bull")
        if isinstance(res, dict):
            def keep(items):
                good = []
                for it in items or []:
                    if isinstance(it, dict):
                        refs = [r for r in it.get("refs") or [] if r in valid]
                        if refs:
                            good.append({**it, "refs": refs})
                return good
            out.update(narrative=keep(res.get("narrative")), bull=keep(res.get("bull")), bear=keep(res.get("bear")),
                       watch=res.get("watch") or [], oneLiner=res.get("oneLiner"), method="llm")
    if out["method"] == "rules":
        # Deterministic fallback: sort computed facts into supportive vs worrying by keywords.
        for fid, t in facts:
            low = t.lower()
            if any(k in low for k in ("pressure", "not showing up", "lengthening", "jumped", "highly geared",
                                      "compressing", "holding down", "lagged")):
                out["bear"].append({"point": t, "refs": [fid]})
            elif any(k in low for k in ("operating leverage", "turning into cash", "improving", "lightly geared",
                                        "compounded", "expanding", "holding up")):
                out["bull"].append({"point": t, "refs": [fid]})
    if not (llm.enabled and out["method"] == "rules"):  # don't pin a fallback answer when the LLM merely failed
        store.set("thesis", key, out)
    return out

Contents of https://cloud.google.com/run/pricing:
## Cloud Run pricing

Cloud Run charges you only for the resources you use, rounded up to the nearest 100 millisecond. Your total Cloud Run bill will be the sum of the resource usage in the pricing table after the free tier is applied.

When setting [concurrency](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-concurrency) higher than one request at a time, multiple requests can share the allocated CPU and memory of an instance.

Outbound internet data transfer uses the [Premium Network Service Tier](https://cloud.google.com/network-tiers/docs/overview#premium_tier) and is charged at [Google Cloud networking pricing](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing) with a free tier of 1GiB free data transfer within North America per month.

Data transfer to Virtual Private Cloud networks is billed as Data transfer from a VM and charged at [Virtual Private Cloud data transfer rates](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing#egress). Serverless VPC Access connectors also charge for the compute required to run them. See [Serverless VPC Access pricing](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing#serverless-vpc-pricing).

There is no charge for data transfer to Google Cloud resources in the same region (for example for traffic from one Cloud Run service to another Cloud Run service). There is no charge for data transfer to [Media CDN](https://cloud.google.com/media-cdn/docs), [Cloud CDN](https://cloud.google.com/cdn/docs), and [Cloud Load Balancing](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing).

## Pricing considerations

When evaluating the pricing of Cloud Run, consider the following:

*   **On-demand and pay per use**: Cloud Run provides on-demand capacity and automatically scales instances. Cloud Run does not require pre-provisioning infrastructure to accommodate for anticipated peak usage. Container instances billed by Cloud Run are used container instances.
*   **Total cost of ownership**: While Cloud Run charges for compute costs, Cloud Run provides more value. For example, Cloud Run offers [zonal redundancy](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/zonal-redundancy), requires low operations because [Site Reliability Engineers](https://sre.google/) do a lot in the background, and makes you and your team more productive via its simplicity.
*   **Committed use discounts**: The cost of any continuous use of Cloud Run can be lowered by purchasing [committed use discounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/cud). For example, if your Cloud Run service always has one or more active instances, you can lower its cost by committing to at least this amount. Compute flexible committed use discounts apply across GKE, Compute Engine and Cloud Run.

Read more about [cost optimization](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/tips/services-cost-optimization).

### Pricing calculator

## Pricing tables

The following pricing tables use the _GiB-second_ unit. A GiB-second means for example running a 1 gibibyte instance for 1 second, or running a 256 mebibyte instance for 4 seconds. The same principle applies for the _vCPU-second_ unit. CUD refers to [committed use discounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/cud).

The free tier usage is aggregated across [projects](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects) by [billing account](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/manage-billing-account) and resets every month; you are billed only for usage past the free tier. The free tier is applied as a spending based discount using Tier 1 pricing.

Cloud Run pricing depends on the [selected region](https://cloud.google.com/run/pricing#tiers). Pricing for Cloud Run services also depends on the [billing](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/billing-settings) configuration.

If you pay in a currency other than USD, the prices listed in your currency on [Cloud Platform SKUs](https://cloud.google.com/skus/) apply.

### Services (Instance-based billing)

I'm seeing two uvicorn processes bound near port 8081 — the new offline2 instance holding the listener, while an older process seems to have lingered even after being stopped, suggesting the stop command may not have fully killed its child python process. Actually, this matches the venv launcher pattern on Windows: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` is just a redirector that spawns the real base python.exe as a child, so both processes likely share the same command line and belong to the same offline2 instance, not two separate servers. That explains the earlier copy failure too — the previous instance was probably still mid-shutdown when I copied finn.db, leaving stale -wal/-shm files that got paired with the fresh db copy, risking a WAL replay mismatch since the WAL header's salt wouldn't match the new db file. Q:\sp\finn\README.md (lines 1-40)
# FINN - Financial Investment Agent

A mobile-first prototype for a portfolio manager covering Indian equities. Two jobs:

- **Push - "what needs me?"** Everything the exchanges published about your holdings, folded into a short brief: what matters first, why it's there, and the numbers already pulled out.
- **Pull - "should I believe this company?"** An on-demand dossier for any NSE stock, built only from primary sources. At its centre is a **promise tracker**: what management guided on earnings calls vs. what they then delivered, with a receipt for every verdict.

Screenshots are in [`docs/screenshots`](docs/screenshots). The covering note is in [`docs/WRITEUP.md`](docs/WRITEUP.md), the AI build history in [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md), and every runtime prompt in [`docs/PROMPTS.md`](docs/PROMPTS.md).

---

## Run it (about 2 minutes)

Needs **Python 3.10+**. The built frontend is included, so Node isn't needed.

```powershell
# Windows
.\run.ps1
```
```bash
# macOS / Linux
chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
```

Then open **http://localhost:8000**. The script also prints a LAN address (e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:8000`) to open on a phone on the same Wi-Fi. "Add to Home Screen" installs it as an app (PWA).

**AI is optional.** Put a free Gemini key in `backend/.env` (`GEMINI_API_KEY=...`, from https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) to switch on transcript reading, verdicts, bios and Ask.
- Without a key, FINN runs in **rules mode**: digest, scoring, results tables, alerts and dossier numbers all still work.
- AI analyses already in the shipped cache are replayed, labelled with their date: the research picks LT, PIDILITIND, POLYCAB, DIXON, ASIANPAINT, TRENT.
- Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works instead of Gemini (Groq, OpenRouter, local Ollama); see `backend/.env.example`.

`backend/data/finn.db` is a pre-warmed cache, so the first screen opens instantly. Set `FINN_OFFLINE=1` to demo purely from it.

Frontend development: `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev` (proxies `/api` to port 8000).

---

Your steps:

  1. Install the Google Cloud CLI with winget install Google.CloudSDK, open a new terminal, and run gcloud auth login.

  2. Create a new project at console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate and link a billing account to it. Keep it separate from your Gemini key's project, because enabling billing there would move the key to paid usage. Light demo traffic should stay within the free tier.

  4. Paste the link into the "Try it" line of docs\WRITEUP.md and into your email.

  • If NSE blocks Google's servers: the brief shows the newest filings it has and an amber note saying so, instead of going empty.

  • Protecting your free quota: there's a per-network request limit and a cap of 400 fresh AI calls a day.

  • Your Gemini key: it goes into Google's Secret Manager, never into the uploaded code.
